knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic certified partition workflow for compact DC minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a finite active partition \(\mathcal P_k\) of a compact feasible set, a feasible incumbent \(U_k\), and valid bounds \(L(B)\leq\inf_{x\in B}f(x)\). Discard cells satisfying \(L(B)\geq U_k\), subdivide a remaining cell into finitely many covering cells, compute their bounds and feasible trial values, and stop with an \(\varepsilon\)-global incumbent when \(U_k-\min_{B\in\mathcal P_k}L(B)\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition the feasible region, lower-bound each cell, prune cells that cannot improve the incumbent, and stop when the certified global gap reaches tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The feasible set is nonempty and compact.
Active cells cover every feasible point not already safely fathomed.
Every \(L(B)\) is a valid finite regional lower bound.
Every incumbent value is attained at a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_k-\min_{B\in\mathcal P_k}L(B)\leq\varepsilon\Longrightarrow U_k-\min f\leq\varepsilon.

notation.meaning: Valid lower bound on cell B.
Best feasible value through iteration k.

knowledge_statements.title: DC Partition Search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regional consistency condition required for asymptotic partition convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every infinite nested selected-cell sequence \(B_k\) has \(\operatorname{diam}(B_k)\to0\) and satisfies \[0\leq\inf_{x\in B_k}f(x)-L(B_k)\leq\eta(\operatorname{diam}(B_k)),\qquad \eta(t)\to0\text{ as }t\downarrow0.\] Then \(\inf_{B_k}f-L(B_k)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regional DC bounds are consistent when their error is controlled by a modulus vanishing with cell diameter.
assumptions_latex: \(L(B)\) is a valid finite lower bound on every active cell.
Every infinite nested selected-cell sequence has vanishing diameter.
The displayed error estimate holds for a function \(\eta\) with \(\eta(t)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{x\in B_k}f(x)-L(B_k)\to0.

notation.meaning: Cells along an infinite nested selected sequence.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Consistency for DC Partitioning

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cellwise DC Minorant from a Convex Majorant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical regional convex lower model used by DC partition search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f=g-h\) on a convex cell \(B\), with \(g\) and \(h\) convex. If the affine function \(a_B\) satisfies \(a_B(x)\geq h(x)\) on \(B\), then \(\underline f_B=g-a_B\) is convex and satisfies \(\underline f_B\leq f\) on \(B\). Therefore \(L(B)=\inf_{x\in B}\underline f_B(x)\) is a valid regional lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine majorant of the subtracted convex component produces a convex cellwise lower model.
assumptions_latex: \(a_B\) is an affine majorant of \(h\) on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \underline f_B=g-a_B\text{ is convex and }\underline f_B\leq f\text{ on }B.

notation.meaning: Affine majorant of the subtracted convex component.

knowledge_statements.title: Cellwise DC Minorant from a Convex Majorant

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Convergence of Consistent Best-Bound DC Partitioning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global convergence under exhaustive refinement, consistent bounds, and adequate feasible sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the DC partition search, suppose cells are selected by best bound, every infinite selected nested sequence has vanishing diameter and consistent bounds, and feasible trial values on such a sequence approach the objective value at its feasible limit. If the algorithm does not terminate earlier, then the global active lower bounds and incumbent values converge to the global minimum; consequently every positive absolute-gap tolerance is eventually attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Best-bound DC partitioning converges globally when refinement is exhaustive, cell bounds are consistent, and feasible sampling tracks refined cells.
assumptions_latex: The assumptions of DC Partition Search hold and \(f\) is continuous on the compact feasible set.
A cell attaining the least active lower bound is selected at every nonterminal iteration.
Every infinite selected nested-cell sequence has vanishing diameter and consistent regional bounds.
Feasible trial values generated along every such sequence converge to the objective at its feasible limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{B\in\mathcal P_k}L(B)\to f^*,\qquad U_k\to f^*.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Convergence of Consistent Best-Bound DC Partitioning

assumptions_latex: \(f=g-h\) on \(X\), where \(g,h:X\to\mathbb{R}\) are convex and continuous.
Every partition cell admits a computable convex underestimator of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If cells with lower bound below the incumbent are selected fairly and the maximum diameter of every infinite nested selected-cell sequence tends to zero, then every accumulation point of incumbents is globally minimizing.

notation.meaning: current finite partition of the feasible set
valid lower bound on a cell
best feasible objective value found through iteration k

4.7 Convex Minorants of a DC Function p. 117

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a finite partition \(\mathcal P_0=\{X\}\), a feasible incumbent \(U_0=f(x^0)\), and valid cell bounds \(L(B)\leq\min_{x\in B}f(x)\). At iteration \(k\), discard every \(B\in\mathcal P_k\) satisfying \(L(B)\geq U_k\). Select a remaining cell, subdivide it into finitely many compact convex cells, compute their bounds and feasible trial points, and set \(U_{k+1}\) to the least observed value. Stop with an \(\varepsilon\)-global solution when \(U_k-\min_{B\in\mathcal P_k}L(B)\leq\varepsilon\); otherwise continue subdivision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition the feasible region, bound each cell from below, prune cells that cannot improve the incumbent, and refine until the global optimality gap is at most epsilon.

children.title: Difference-of-Convex Reformulations
children.top_down_role: Representation choices that expose DC structure for global search.

knowledge_statements.title: Difference-of-Convex Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional DC representation of an objective and finitely many inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\in\mathbb N\). A DC program has the form \(\min_{x\in X}\{g_0(x)-h_0(x):g_i(x)-h_i(x)\leq0,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\). Introducing \(t\in\mathbb R\) gives the epigraph formulation \[\min_{x\in X,\,t\in\mathbb R} t-h_0(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g_0(x)\leq t,\quad g_i(x)-h_i(x)\leq0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m).\] For every feasible \(x\) of the original problem, choosing \(t=g_0(x)\) gives the same objective value, while every feasible \((x,t)\) of the epigraph problem satisfies \(t-h_0(x)\geq g_0(x)-h_0(x)\). Hence the two problems have the same infimum, and whenever an optimum is attained their optimal \(x\)-components coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Express the objective and each inequality as a difference of two convex functions. An epigraph variable for the positive convex objective component produces a formulation with the same optimal value and the same optimal x-components when optima exist.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i,h_i:X\to\mathbb R\) are finite-valued convex functions for \(i=0,1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original and epigraph formulations have the same infimum; when an optimum is attained, their minimizing \(x\)-components coincide.

notation.meaning: convex components of inequality constraint i
epigraph variable for the positive convex objective component

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Difference of Convex (D.C.) Functions p. 58
4.7 Convex Minorants of a DC Function p. 117

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding the same convex function to both components preserves the represented DC function.
assumptions_latex: \(g,h,\phi\) are convex on a common convex domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f=(g+\phi)-(h+\phi).

notation.meaning: Common convex term added to both components.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: DC Equality as Two DC Inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact inequality-only representation of a DC equality constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For convex \(g,h\), \[g(x)-h(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad g(x)-h(x)\leq0,\quad h(x)-g(x)\leq0.\] Both inequalities are DC constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A DC equality is exactly equivalent to its two opposite DC inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) and \(h\) are finite convex functions on a common domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: g(x)-h(x)=0\Longleftrightarrow\bigl[g(x)-h(x)\leq0\ \wedge\ h(x)-g(x)\leq0\bigr].

children.title: Relaxation-Strength Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where decomposition or partition choices yield weak global bounds.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Arbitrarily Weak and Inconsistent Equivalent DC Decompositions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposition-dependent relaxation failure on fixed and shrinking intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f\equiv0\) on \(B=[-r,r]\), write \(f(x)=Mx^2-Mx^2\). The endpoint secant majorant of \(h(x)=Mx^2\) is \(a_B(x)=Mr^2\), so \(\underline f_B(x)=Mx^2-Mr^2\) and \(\min_B f-\min_B\underline f_B=Mr^2\). On the fixed interval \(r=1\), this gap is arbitrarily large as \(M\to\infty\). On shrinking intervals, choosing \(M=r^{-2}\) keeps the gap equal to one even as \(r\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent DC decompositions can make a bound arbitrarily weak, and changing the decomposition with the cell can prevent consistency even on shrinking cells.
assumptions_latex: The subtracted convex quadratic is replaced by its endpoint secant majorant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_B f-\min_B\underline f_B=Mr^2;\quad M=r^{-2}\Longrightarrow\text{gap}=1.

notation.meaning: Scaling of the common convex quadratic.
Affine secant majorant of the subtracted component.

knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrarily Weak and Inconsistent Equivalent DC Decompositions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restriction Monotonicity with a Fixed DC Lower Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strength improvement under spatial restriction when the lower model is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(B'\subseteq B\) and the same valid lower model \(\underline f_B\leq f\) is used on both cells, then \[\inf_{x\in B'}\underline f_B(x)\geq\inf_{x\in B}\underline f_B(x).\] Hence domain restriction cannot weaken a fixed relaxation; parent-child bound monotonicity may fail only when the model, its decomposition, or its parameters are changed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shrinking a cell strengthens a fixed lower model, whereas rebuilding the model can reverse bound monotonicity.
assumptions_latex: \(\underline f_B\) is a valid lower model on \(B\) and is reused on \(B'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{B'}\underline f_B\geq\inf_B\underline f_B.
knowledge_statements.title: Restriction Monotonicity with a Fixed DC Lower Model

assumptions_latex: \(B\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) is a compact convex cell with diameter \(d(B)\).
\(f=g-h\) on \(B\), with \(g\) convex and \(h\) convex and Lipschitz with constant \(M_B\).
\(\ell_B\) is an affine minorant of \(-h\) on \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation error is bounded by \(0\leq f(x)-\underline f_B(x)\leq2M_Bd(B)\) for every \(x\in B\), so diameter reduction forces consistency, whereas nonshrinking cells need not yield exact bounds.

notation.meaning: Lipschitz constant of h on B

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency boundary for cellwise DC convex relaxations under Lipschitz control.

source_refs.locator: 4.7 Convex Minorants of a DC Function p. 117
11.2 Convex Lower Bounding Function p. 318

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\ell_B(x)\leq-h(x)\) on \(B\) and that \(\ell_B\) touches \(-h\) at some \(z_B\in B\). Then \(\underline f_B=g+\ell_B\) is convex and satisfies \(\underline f_B\leq f\) on \(B\). Since both \(h\) and the touching affine support have slopes bounded in norm by \(M_B\), \[0\leq f(x)-\underline f_B(x)\leq2M_Bd(B),\qquad x\in B.\] Thus nested cells with \(d(B_k)\to0\) have vanishing relaxation error. Without shrinking diameters or uniform local slope control, the relaxation gap may remain positive, so pruning based on asymptotic exactness is unjustified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DC lower bounds become exact on shrinking cells under local Lipschitz control; without shrinking or slope control, a persistent relaxation gap can defeat global certification.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Strength Boundaries

At stage \(k\), construct a transformed trajectory \(y_k(t)=T_k(x_k^*,t)\) that leaves the basin already represented by \(x_k^*\). Select an admissible point \(y_k(t_k)\), compute \(x_{k+1}=\mathcal L(y_k(t_k))\), and set \(x_{k+1}^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{f(x_k^*),f(x_{k+1})\}\). children.title: Generalized-Descent Search
children.top_down_role: Search families extending descent concepts beyond ordinary local improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized-Descent Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalized descent alternating value-nonincreasing local minimization with attempts at strict interbasin escape.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(y_0\in X\), set \(x_0=\mathcal L(y_0)\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), call \(\mathcal E(x_k)\). If it returns \(y_k\in X\) with \(f(y_k)<f(x_k)\), set \(x_{k+1}=\mathcal L(y_k)\); then \(f(x_{k+1})\leq f(y_k)<f(x_k)\). If it certifies that \(\{z\in X:f(z)<f(x_k)\}=\varnothing\), stop and output \(x_k\) as a global minimizer. If it fails without that certificate, stop or continue according to the prescribed search policy, but regard \(x_k\) only as an uncertified incumbent. Thus generalized descent requires strict improvement between accepted local minima, while global optimality requires a complete escape certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generalized descent alternates value-nonincreasing local optimization with attempts to enter a strictly better basin. Failure establishes global optimality only when the escape procedure certifies that no lower-valued feasible point exists.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact and \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
The local minimization operator \(\mathcal L:X\to X\) returns a local minimizer and satisfies \(f(\mathcal L(y))\leq f(y)\) for every \(y\in X\).

At a local minimizer \(x\), the escape operator \(\mathcal E\) returns either a point \(y\in X\) with \(f(y)<f(x)\), a valid certificate that no such point exists, or an explicitly uncertified failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every successful outer iteration strictly decreases the accepted local-minimum value; global optimality follows only from a valid certificate that no point in \(X\) has value below the incumbent.

notation.meaning: escape operator based at an accepted local minimizer
accepted local minimizer at iteration k

source_refs.locator: 3. Methods of Generalized Descent p. 53

source_witnesses.locator: 3. Methods of Generalized Descent p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Descent over Finitely Many Local-Minimum Levels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Successful-transition bound when generalized descent can accept only finitely many distinct local-minimum objective levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\{f(x):x\text{ is an eligible local minimizer}\}\) have \(m<\infty\) distinct values. If each successful generalized-descent transition accepts \(x_{k+1}\) only when \(f(x_{k+1})<f(x_k)\), then any run contains at most \(m-1\) successful transitions. This bound does not imply that an unsuccessful escape attempt is a global-optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With only m eligible local-minimum levels, strict generalized descent can make at most m minus one successful transitions; an ensuing failed escape is still uncertified unless it excludes every lower-valued feasible point.
assumptions_latex: \(V=\{f(x):x\text{ is an eligible local minimizer}\}\) has \(m<\infty\) distinct values.

notation.meaning: set of eligible local-minimum objective levels
number of distinct values in V

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Descent over Finitely Many Local-Minimum Levels

children.title: Local-to-Global Transitions
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms governing movement from local improvement into broader exploration.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in X\) is a local minimizer returned by a local solver.
The escape test is complete for the strict sublevel set below \(f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transition from local to global status occurs exactly when the strict lower sublevel set is empty: \(S_x=\varnothing\iff x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in X}f(z)\).

notation.meaning: strict sublevel set below the current local-minimum value

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact value-based condition converting a local minimizer into a global certificate.

source_refs.locator: 2.5 Local, Global, epsilon-Global Minima p. 57
5.1 Global vs. Local Optimum p. 127

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(S_x=\{z\in X:f(z)<f(x)\}\). Then \[x\in X^*:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in X}f(z)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad S_x=\varnothing.\] Hence an escape procedure converts the local conclusion at \(x\) into a global conclusion precisely when it searches \(S_x\) completely and certifies emptiness. More generally, if it certifies \(f(z)\geq f(x)-\varepsilon\) for every \(z\in X\), then \(x\) is \(\varepsilon\)-global, meaning \(f(x)\leq\min_{z\in X}f(z)+\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local minimizer becomes globally certified exactly when no feasible point has lower value; excluding values more than epsilon lower yields epsilon-global certification.
knowledge_statements.title: Local-to-Global Transitions

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5 Local, Global, epsilon-Global Minima p. 57
5.1 Global vs. Local Optimum p. 127

children.title: Trajectory Stagnation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Path structures that trap or stall trajectory-based global search.

assumptions_latex: The trajectory rule generates trial points only in a subset \(R\subseteq X\).
A better basin contains a nonempty relatively open set \(V\subseteq X\setminus\overline R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No generated trajectory point enters \(V\); therefore a local solver launched only from the trajectory cannot discover the better minimizer in that basin.

notation.meaning: reachable set of the trajectory rule
unreached portion of an improving attraction basin

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reachability failure causing deterministic transformed trajectories to miss improving basins.

source_refs.locator: 3. Methods of Generalized Descent p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let every trial point generated from the incumbent \(x^c\) lie in \(R\), and suppose \(V\subseteq X\setminus\overline R\) lies in the attraction basin of a local minimizer \(x^b\) with \(f(x^b)<f(x^c)\). Then no trajectory launch belongs to \(V\), so repeated local searches restricted to those launches cannot reach \(x^b\) through \(V\). Stagnation may therefore occur even when objective values along the generated path decrease locally. A global convergence claim requires a reachability, density, exhaustive-restart, or valid lower-bound condition that rules out such hidden improving basins.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trajectory stagnates globally when its reachable set misses an open part of every route into a better basin, even if it continues making local progress.
knowledge_statements.title: Trajectory Stagnation Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 3. Methods of Generalized Descent p. 53

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Missing one relatively open subset V of an attraction basin does not prevent other reachable launches from entering the same basin and finding its minimizer. A valid failure result needs the whole relevant launch region or every route into the improving basin to be unreachable, with a direct supporting locator.

children.title: Homotopy Global Methods
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for parameterized continuation approaches to global search.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A regular continuation path can be followed to a zero of \(H(\cdot,1)\), but global optimization additionally requires an endpoint-selection or exhaustive-path condition linking terminal zeros to global minimizers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic regular continuation scheme; the intended global-selection mechanism remains source-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \((x_0,\lambda_0)=(x_0,0)\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), predict a point on the solution manifold \(H(x,\lambda)=0\) using a tangent satisfying \(D_xH\,\dot x+D_\lambda H\,\dot\lambda=0\), then correct it by solving \(H(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})=0\). Adapt the step size and continue until \(\lambda_{k+1}=1\). If \(D_xH(x(\lambda),\lambda)\) is nonsingular along the path, local continuation is well-defined. Output a terminal point only after applying the method's prescribed rule for selecting globally minimizing endpoints or exhausting all relevant paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Homotopy methods track solutions from an easy parameter value to the target problem; regular tracking alone does not ensure that the selected endpoint is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Homotopy Global Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This immutable node is a topic-level navigation container, not an exact algorithm leaf. The generic predictor-corrector continuation algorithm therefore does not fit the container, and no source identifies a specific global homotopy method or endpoint-selection guarantee.

children.title: Local-Minimum Escape Transformations
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for transformations designed to escape known local minima.

children.title: Tunneling Transformations
children.top_down_role: Landscape transformations designed to move search beyond a known local minimizer.

assumptions_latex: The transformed search excludes \(x^c\) and points where \(f(x)=f(x^c)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every negative value of \(T_p\) identifies a point strictly better than \(x^c\); thus minimizing the transform can provide an escape from the incumbent level set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pole-based tunneling transform for detecting points below an incumbent local-minimum level.

source_refs.locator: 3. Methods of Generalized Descent p. 53

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in X\setminus\{x^c\}\) with \(f(x)\neq f(x^c)\), define \[T_p(x;x^c)=\frac{f(x)-f(x^c)}{\lVert x-x^c\rVert^p}.\] Because the denominator is positive, \(T_p(x;x^c)<0\) if and only if \(f(x)<f(x^c)\). Consequently, any feasible point with negative transformed value is a directly verifiable escape point. The pole at \(x^c\) discourages return to the incumbent, while the transformation preserves the sign of improvement; it does not by itself guarantee that a local minimization of \(T_p\) will find a negative value when one exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pole-based transform has negative value exactly at points better than the current local minimizer, so finding a negative transformed value certifies an escape.
knowledge_statements.title: Tunneling Transformations

source_witnesses.locator: 3. Methods of Generalized Descent p. 53

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sign equivalence of the displayed quotient is elementary, but calling the singularity a pole that discourages return is not valid for every p>0; its limiting behavior depends on p and the local growth of f. The specific tunneling transformation and admissible exponent require direct source confirmation.

children.title: Filled-Function Transformations
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary-landscape families designed to suppress attraction to known local minima.

assumptions_latex: \(x^c\) is a nonglobal local minimizer of \(f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local minimization of a filled function cannot terminate at a nonincumbent point in the old basin and, when it reaches a point below the incumbent level, supplies an escape start for minimizing \(f\).

notation.meaning: attraction basin of the incumbent under the fixed local solver
filled function based at the incumbent
strict lower sublevel set of the incumbent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational filled-function definition relative to a fixed local solver and incumbent basin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B(x^c)\) be the attraction basin of \(x^c\) for a fixed local solver and let \(S_{x^c}=\{x\in X:f(x)<f(x^c)\}\). A function \(P(\cdot;x^c):X\to\mathbb{R}\) is a filled function at \(x^c\) if \(x^c\) is a strict local maximizer of \(P\), \(P\) has no local minimizer in \(B(x^c)\setminus\{x^c\}\), and every local minimizer of \(P\) reachable from a descent launch outside the incumbent satisfies or leads to \(S_{x^c}\). The transformation fills the incumbent basin while preserving an avenue toward a strictly lower objective level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filled function turns the current minimizer into a local maximum, removes competing minima from its basin, and directs transformed descent toward a lower objective level.
knowledge_statements.title: Filled-Function Transformations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Filled-function definitions impose source-dependent properties, and the clause that every reachable local minimizer 'satisfies or leads to' the lower sublevel set is not mathematically defined. A direct definition or theorem locator is required.

children.title: Escape-Basin Selection
children.top_down_role: Structural choices governing which neighboring basins become reachable.

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact and partitioned into attraction basins for a fixed deterministic local solver.
A finite candidate set \(Y_k\subset X\) and valid basin lower estimates are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Discarding only basins whose valid lower estimate is at least \(f(x^c)\) preserves every improving basin; fair selection among the remaining candidates eventually launches in each represented improving basin.

notation.meaning: finite candidate launch set at iteration k
estimated or identified basin containing y
valid lower estimate for a basin

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fair basin selection using valid lower estimates and transformed candidate launches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), remove every \(y\in Y_k\) whose basin is already explored or satisfies \(L(B(y))\geq f(x^c)\). From the remaining candidates select \[y_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in Y_k}L(B(y)),\] breaking ties by a fair rule. Apply the local solver at \(y_k\); if it returns \(x^{\mathrm{new}}\) with \(f(x^{\mathrm{new}})<f(x^c)\), replace the incumbent. Mark \(B(y_k)\) explored and augment \(Y_k\) using the prescribed escape transformation. Stop globally only when every unvisited basin has a valid lower estimate at least \(f(x^c)\); otherwise return an uncertified incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select an unexplored basin with the best valid lower estimate, launch local search there, and certify globality only after all remaining basin bounds exceed the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Escape-Basin Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed algorithm assumes identifiable attraction basins and valid lower bounds for each basin, neither of which is defined or sourced. Its fairness and eventual-coverage conclusion also requires a precise rule governing candidate-set augmentation and basin representation.

children.title: Transformation Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where transformed landscapes fail to reveal useful escape directions.

assumptions_latex: A local escape transformation is searched only inside a neighborhood contained in the attraction basin of the right-hand local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transformation may certify no local escape while the left-hand local minimizer has strictly smaller objective value; hence incomplete transformed search cannot certify global optimality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete double-well failure caused by restricting transformed search to the incumbent basin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For sufficiently small \(\delta>0\), the tilted double-well function \(f(x)=(x^2-1)^2+\delta x\) has two strict local minimizers \(x_L<0<x_R\), with \(f(x_L)<f(x_R)\). Let a tunneling or filled-function subproblem be solved only on a closed neighborhood \(N_R\) contained in the attraction basin of \(x_R\) and disjoint from the strict sublevel set \(\{x:f(x)<f(x_R)\}\). Then no transformed trial restricted to \(N_R\) can reveal \(x_L\), although \(x_R\) is nonglobal. Failure of this restricted transformation therefore supplies no global certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tilted double well defeats an escape transformation confined to the worse well: local failure to escape does not exclude a better minimum elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.title: Transformation Failure Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The tilted double well does exhibit two unequal local minima for a suitable explicit range of delta, but that range is not stated and the claimed behavior is not tied to a defined tunneling or filled-function transformation. A direct source or a transformation-specific formulation is required.

children.title: Randomized Hybrid Search Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Global exploration families using randomized sampling, stochastic transitions, statistical models, or local-search hybrids.

children.title: Random Search Families
children.top_down_role: Foundational randomized global-search architectures.

children.title: Pure Random Search
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for independent global sampling.

assumptions_latex: The feasible region \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is measurable and carries a probability measure \(\mu\).
The objective \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is measurable and bounded below.
For every \(\varepsilon>0\), the near-optimal set \(A_\varepsilon=\{x\in X:f(x)<f^\star+\varepsilon\}\) has positive \(\mu\)-measure, where \(f^\star=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent values satisfy \(f(\widehat X_n)\to f^\star\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: Best sampled point after n evaluations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent identically distributed sampling with incumbent selection on a measurable continuous domain.

source_refs.locator: Section 2.2.1, Pure Random Search and the Associated c.d.f., p. 38
Section 2.1.3, Convergence of Global Random Search Algorithms, p. 34

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n=1,2,\ldots\), independently draw \(X_n\sim\mu\), evaluate \(f(X_n)\), and choose \(\widehat X_n\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i\le n}f(X_i)\) using a fixed tie rule. Under the stated positive-mass condition, the resulting incumbent values converge almost surely to the global infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independently sample from a fixed probability distribution and retain the best sampled point. If every near-optimal set has positive sampling probability, the incumbent value converges almost surely to the global infimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Pure Random Search

source_witnesses.locator: Section 2.2.1, Pure Random Search and the Associated c.d.f., p. 38
Section 2.1.3, Convergence of Global Random Search Algorithms, p. 34

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Near-Optimal Hitting Probability and Evaluation Count
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample performance of independent pure random search for a fixed near-optimal set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_\varepsilon=\{x:f(x)<f^*+\varepsilon\}\) have sampling probability \(p_\varepsilon=\mu(A_\varepsilon)\). For \(n\) independent draws, \[\Pr\!\left(\min_{1\le i\le n}f(X_i)<f^*+\varepsilon\right)=1-(1-p_\varepsilon)^n.\] If \(0<p_\varepsilon<1\), confidence at least \(1-\alpha\) is attained exactly when \((1-p_\varepsilon)^n\le\alpha\), equivalently \[n\ge\left\lceil\frac{\log\alpha}{\log(1-p_\varepsilon)}\right\rceil.\] The first hitting time has mean \(1/p_\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pure random search hits an epsilon-optimal set with probability one minus the corresponding miss probability; expected waiting time is the reciprocal of its sampling mass.
assumptions_latex: \(0<p_\varepsilon<1\) for the displayed finite-count and mean formulas.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr(U_n<f^*+\varepsilon)=1-(1-p_\varepsilon)^n,\qquad \mathbb E[\tau_\varepsilon]=p_\varepsilon^{-1}.

notation.meaning: sampling probability of the epsilon-optimal set
best objective value among the first n samples
first sample index entering the epsilon-optimal set

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Near-Optimal Hitting Probability and Evaluation Count

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure When the Sampling Law Misses the Optimum Region
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp necessity of positive sampling mass for every near-optimal set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]\), \(f(x)=x\), and let every sample be uniform on \([1/2,1]\). Then \(f^*=0\), but all sampled values are at least \(1/2\), and the incumbent values converge almost surely to \(1/2\), not to \(f^*\). Thus the sampling law must charge every near-optimal set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent random search can converge to the best value in its sampling support while missing the true global optimum.
assumptions_latex: Samples are independent and uniform on \([1/2,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_n\to\tfrac12\text{ almost surely while }f^*=0.

notation.meaning: best sampled objective value after n draws

knowledge_statements.title: Failure When the Sampling Law Misses the Optimum Region

children.title: Pure Adaptive Search
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for adaptive restriction of randomized search regions.

assumptions_latex: The feasible region \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is measurable and satisfies \(0<\lambda(X)<\infty\) for a reference measure \(\lambda\).
The measurable objective \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) attains its minimum \(f^\star=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\).
For every \(\varepsilon>0\), the near-optimal set \(A_\varepsilon=\{x\in X:f(x)<f^\star+\varepsilon\}\) has positive \(\lambda\)-measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent values decrease strictly whenever an update occurs and satisfy \(f(Y_n)\to f^\star\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: Strict improving region determined by the incumbent
Reference measure on the feasible region

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Idealized order-one pure adaptive search using uniform sampling from the current improving region.

source_refs.locator: Section 2.2.3, Pure Adaptive Search and Related Methods, p. 48
Section 2.2.4, Pure Adaptive Search of Order k, p. 50

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(Y_0\in X\). At iteration \(n\), define \(R_n=\{x\in X:f(x)<f(Y_n)\}\). If \(R_n=\varnothing\), stop and output \(Y_n\). Otherwise, draw \(Y_{n+1}\) from the probability measure \(\lambda(\cdot\cap R_n)/\lambda(R_n)\). Under the stated positive-measure condition on every near-optimal set, the incumbent values converge almost surely to \(f^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from an incumbent, sample uniformly with respect to the reference measure from its strictly improving region. Updates strictly improve the objective, and positive measure for every near-optimal set yields almost-sure convergence to the global minimum value.
knowledge_statements.title: Pure Adaptive Search

source_witnesses.locator: Section 2.2.3, Pure Adaptive Search and Related Methods, p. 48
Section 2.2.4, Pure Adaptive Search of Order k, p. 50

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pure Adaptive Search of Order k
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-memory order-k variant of the accepted order-one scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain the \(k\) best observations and let \(T_n\) be the worst retained value. Draw the next point from the reference measure conditioned on \(R_n^{(k)}=\{x:f(x)<T_n\}\), insert it, and discard the worst observation so that \(k\) remain. The retained threshold is nonincreasing; \(k=1\) reduces to ordinary pure adaptive search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order-k PAS samples below the current kth-best threshold and retains the k best observations.
assumptions_latex: The improving sublevel set has positive finite measure whenever sampling continues.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{n+1}\le T_n\), and \(k=1\) is the accepted seed algorithm.

notation.meaning: Sublevel region below the kth-best threshold

source_refs.locator: Section 2.2.4, Pure Adaptive Search of Order k, p. 50

knowledge_statements.title: Pure Adaptive Search of Order k

source_witnesses.locator: Section 2.2.4, Pure Adaptive Search of Order k, p. 50

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Logarithmic Iteration Count in Volume Rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact idealized hitting-time law in objective-volume coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the atomless rank representation with \(V_0=1\), let \(\tau_q=\inf\{n\ge1:V_n\le q\}\). Then \(\tau_q-1\) is Poisson distributed with mean \(\log(1/q)\), and \(\mathbb E[\tau_q]=1+\log(1/q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Idealized PAS reaches the best q fraction by objective volume after an expected one plus log one-over-q adaptive draws.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\tau_q-1\sim\operatorname{Poisson}(\log(1/q))\) and \(\mathbb E\tau_q=1+\log(1/q)\).

notation.meaning: First draw reaching volume rank at most q

knowledge_statements.title: Logarithmic Iteration Count in Volume Rank

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates idealized PAS iterations from implementable evaluation complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: PAS presumes exact sampling from \(\lambda(\cdot\cap R_n)/\lambda(R_n)\). If this is implemented by independent uniform proposals on \(X\) rejected outside \(R_n\), the expected proposals for one accepted update equal \(\lambda(X)/\lambda(R_n)\), which can diverge near the optimum. Logarithmic accepted-iteration bounds therefore do not imply logarithmic evaluation complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PAS's idealized rate assumes an exact improving-region sampler; rejection implementations may have reciprocal-volume evaluation cost.
assumptions_latex: Conditional sampling is implemented by uniform proposals on \(X\) and rejection outside \(R_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The expected proposals per accepted update equal \(\lambda(X)/\lambda(R_n)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Sampling Oracle Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative rank representation for idealized order-one PAS.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(V(x)=\lambda(\{z:f(z)<f(x)\})/\lambda(X)\). If this rank is atomless and \(Y_{n+1}\) is uniform on the strict improving region of \(Y_n\), then conditionally on \(V_n=V(Y_n)=v\), \(V_{n+1}\) is uniform on \((0,v)\). Equivalently, \(V_{n+1}=V_nU_{n+1}\) in distribution with independent \(U_{n+1}\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In objective-volume coordinates, idealized order-one PAS multiplies its current rank by an independent uniform factor.
assumptions_latex: Sampling is uniform on each strict improving region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_{n+1}/V_n\sim\operatorname{Unif}(0,1)\) conditionally on the past.

notation.meaning: Relative volume of the strict lower level set

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Volume Quantile Representation

children.title: Coverage-Driven Sampling Search
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for randomized and low-discrepancy coverage schemes.

children.title: Stratified Random Search
children.top_down_role: Random search organized through a partitioned sampling domain.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise finite-design guarantee once every stratum is represented.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\) exactly partition \(X\), choose \(x_j\in S_j\), and set \(\delta=\max_j\operatorname{diam}(S_j)\). For an objective with modulus of continuity \(\omega_f\), \[0\le\min_jf(x_j)-f^\star\le\omega_f(\delta).\] For an \(L\)-Lipschitz objective the bound is \(L\delta\), independently of how representatives were randomized within their strata.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One representative from every exact stratum gives an error bounded by the objective's modulus of continuity at the largest stratum diameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_jf(x_j)-f^\star\le\omega_f(\delta)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Stratum-Diameter Error Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a genuine covering partition and fixes boundary allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite stratification of compact metric space \(X\) is a family of nonempty measurable sets \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\) satisfying \(X=\bigcup_jS_j\) and \(S_i\cap S_j=\varnothing\) for \(i\ne j\), with boundaries assigned explicitly. A one-per-stratum design chooses \(x_j\in S_j\); a randomized design draws \(X_j\) from a distribution supported on \(S_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stratified design exactly partitions the entire domain and selects or samples at least one representative from every stratum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every point, including boundary points, belongs to a represented stratum.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Stratified Design

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for worst-case continuous-objective coverage claims.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A partition only up to reference-measure zero need not cover every possible minimizer. If an omitted point is positively separated from all represented sets, a continuous objective can have its unique minimum there while sampled values remain separated from the optimum. Even for an exact partition, the diameter certificate fails if a stratum receives no representative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting a separated null-set point or leaving a stratum unrepresented can destroy worst-case optimization coverage.
assumptions_latex: A point is omitted and positively separated from represented sets, or some exact stratum has no representative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consistency for every continuous objective and the diameter certificate need not hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Omitted-Set and Unrepresented-Stratum Failures

assumptions_latex: The compact region \(X\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is partitioned into measurable strata \(S_{n,1},\ldots,S_{n,m_n}\).
Each stratum has positive reference measure and its conditional sampling distribution has support equal to that stratum.
The maximal stratum diameter tends to zero as the total number of evaluations grows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every continuous \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\), the best sampled value converges almost surely to \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One conditionally independent draw per shrinking measurable stratum, with best-so-far output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At stage \(n\), construct a partition \(X=\bigcup_{j=1}^{m_n}S_{n,j}\) up to null sets. Independently for each \(j\), draw \(X_{n,j}\) from the reference measure conditioned on \(S_{n,j}\), evaluate \(f(X_{n,j})\), and return the best point among all samples generated through stage \(n\). If \(\delta_n=\max_j\operatorname{diam}(S_{n,j})\to0\), then every point of \(X\) lies arbitrarily close to a sampled stratum representative. Uniform continuity of \(f\) on compact \(X\) consequently yields convergence of the best sampled value to the global minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition the domain into increasingly fine strata, sample once within each stratum, and retain the best evaluation; shrinking strata ensure consistency for continuous objectives.
knowledge_statements.title: Stratified Random Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited. Moreover, a partition only up to null sets need not cover a minimizer located in an omitted null set, so the stated assumptions do not establish the claimed consistency for every continuous objective. The statement also contains proof text. The algorithm kind otherwise fits the leaf.

children.title: Quasirandom Search
children.top_down_role: Global exploration based on low-discrepancy sampling designs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converts declared fill-distance or star-discrepancy rates into objective error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a design prefix has fill distance \(h_n\le Ca_n\), then for modulus of continuity \(\omega_f\), \[0\le\min_{i\le n}f(u_i)-f^\star\le\omega_f(Ca_n).\] On \([0,1]^d\), the bound \(h_n\le2(D_n^*)^{1/d}\) gives error at most \(\omega_f(2(D_n^*)^{1/d})\). For an \(L\)-Hölder objective of exponent \(\alpha\), this is at most \(L2^\alpha(D_n^*)^{\alpha/d}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasirandom prefix's covering or discrepancy rate converts through the objective's modulus of continuity into a deterministic optimization-error rate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuous on the compact unit cube.
The stated fill-distance or discrepancy bound holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_n-f^\star\le\omega_f(h_n)\le\omega_f(2(D_n^*)^{1/d})\).
knowledge_statements.title: Quasirandom Coverage-to-Optimization Rate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard quantitative design class for quasirandom search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence \((u_i)_{i\ge1}\subset[0,1]^d\) is low discrepancy with respect to anchored boxes when its prefix star discrepancies satisfy \(D_n^*=O(n^{-1}(\log n)^d)\). More generally, \(D_n^*\to0\) is equivalent to uniform distribution of the sequence on the unit cube.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Low-discrepancy sequences have rapidly vanishing anchored-box discrepancy; vanishing star discrepancy characterizes uniform distribution.
assumptions_latex: \(D_n^*\) is the star discrepancy of the first \(n\) points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Low discrepancy implies \(D_n^*\to0\) and uniform distribution.
knowledge_statements.title: Low-Discrepancy Sequence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits conclusions drawn merely from labeling a design randomized or low discrepancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Random shifting or scrambling supports pathwise optimization convergence only when the selected construction preserves a deterministic or almost-sure vanishing-discrepancy or vanishing-covering guarantee. Randomization alone supplies no such guarantee. Likewise, discrepancy affects pointwise optimization only through a valid discrepancy-to-covering conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomization alone does not ensure coverage, and discrepancy must be converted geometrically before it bounds optimization error.
assumptions_latex: Only randomization or an unquantified discrepancy label is known.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No pathwise optimization-error guarantee follows without a construction-specific coverage implication.
knowledge_statements.title: Construction-Specific Randomization Boundary

assumptions_latex: The deterministic or randomized point sequence has covering radius tending to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent values satisfy \(\min_{1\le i\le n}f(U_i)\to\min_{x\in X}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Covering radius in the chosen norm
Best objective value through evaluation n

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic low-dispersion sequences or randomized variants used as global-search evaluation sites.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select a space-filling sequence \((U_i)_{i\ge1}\subset[0,1]^d\), such as a low-discrepancy sequence, optionally after a random digital shift or scrambling that preserves its coverage order. Evaluate \(f(U_n)\) sequentially and output an index \(i_n\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i\le n}f(U_i)\). If its covering radius \(h_n\to0\), then for a minimizer \(x^\star\) there is a sampled point within distance \(h_n\) of \(x^\star\). Hence continuity gives \(f(U_{i_n})\to f(x^\star)\). Randomization changes the sampling law but not this conclusion whenever \(h_n\to0\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate a space-filling low-discrepancy sequence and retain its best point; vanishing covering radius guarantees convergence for continuous objectives.
knowledge_statements.title: Quasirandom Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No authoritative source or locator is supplied. The record does not define which low-discrepancy or randomized sequence constructions guarantee the asserted covering-radius behavior, especially almost surely after randomization. The statement also includes a proof sketch. The algorithm kind fits the search-method leaf.

children.title: Randomized Covering Search
children.top_down_role: Randomized schemes designed to improve geometric coverage of the domain.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable probabilistic condition implying almost-sure candidate-pool density.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(C_n\) consists of \(m_n\) iid draws from a full-support probability measure \(\mu\) on compact \(X\). For every rational \(\varepsilon>0\), choose a finite cover by \(K_\varepsilon\) balls of radius \(\varepsilon/2\), and let \(p_\varepsilon>0\) be the smallest \(\mu\)-mass of those balls. If \(\sum_nK_\varepsilon(1-p_\varepsilon)^{m_n}<\infty\) for every such \(\varepsilon\), then \(q_n\to0\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-support candidate pools become dense almost surely when pool sizes make the probabilities of missing finite ball covers summable.
assumptions_latex: Draws within each pool are iid from a full-support measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_n\to0\) almost surely.

notation.meaning: Smallest ball mass in the chosen cover

knowledge_statements.title: Random Candidate-Pool Density Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp support boundary for randomized covering search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every candidate pool is almost surely contained in a closed proper subset \(S\subsetneq X\), every selected site belongs to \(D_{n_0}\cup S\). If some \(x\in X\) has positive distance from that set, then \(\inf_n h(D_n)>0\). Maximin selection therefore cannot repair missing support in the candidate generator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Farthest-candidate selection cannot cover regions that the candidate generator never proposes.
assumptions_latex: \(C_n\subset S\) almost surely for a closed proper subset \(S\subsetneq X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive distance from \(D_{n_0}\cup S\) forces fill distance to remain positive.

notation.meaning: Support subset of all candidate pools

knowledge_statements.title: Missing Candidate Support Prevents Coverage

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dense Candidate Pools Yield Approximate Farthest-Point Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition for maximin candidate selection to generate a dense evaluated design.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact, \(r_n(x)=\operatorname{dist}(x,D_n)\), and choose \(x_{n+1}\in C_n\) satisfying \(r_n(x_{n+1})\ge\sup_{x\in C_n}r_n(x)-\eta_n\). If \(q_n=\sup_{x\in X}\operatorname{dist}(x,C_n)\to0\) and \(\eta_n\to0\), then the evaluated-design fill distance \(h(D_n)=\sup_{x\in X}r_n(x)\) tends to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate farthest-candidate selection becomes dense when candidate pools become dense and selection error vanishes.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Candidate Pools Yield Approximate Farthest-Point Coverage

assumptions_latex: The feasible region \(X\) is compact in a metric space \((X,\rho)\).
At iteration \(n\), a finite random candidate set \(C_n\subset X\) is generated.
Candidate sets become sufficiently dense so that their fill distance tends to zero almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(f\) is continuous, the best evaluated value converges almost surely to \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Distance from a point to the current design
Random candidate set at iteration n

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random candidate generation followed by a maximin coverage rule and incumbent selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an initial finite design \(D_{n_0}\subset X\). For \(n\ge n_0\), generate a finite random candidate set \(C_n\), select \(X_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in C_n}r_n(x)\), evaluate \(f(X_{n+1})\), and set \(D_{n+1}=D_n\cup\{X_{n+1}\}\). Output a minimizer of \(f\) over \(D_n\). If the resulting fill distance \(h(D_n)=\sup_{x\in X}\min_{z\in D_n}\rho(x,z)\) tends to zero almost surely, then compactness and continuity imply that the incumbent objective value converges almost surely to the global minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate random candidates, evaluate the candidate farthest from prior sites, and retain the best point; vanishing fill distance yields global consistency.
knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Covering Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied, and the random candidate-generation assumptions are replaced by the conclusion-like premise that the resulting fill distance tends to zero. A source is needed for a checkable candidate-generation condition that yields coverage. The statement also contains proof text. The algorithm kind fits.

children.title: Coverage Discrepancy Regimes
children.top_down_role: Coverage quality under differing dimension, sample-budget, or design conditions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cube-specific curse-of-dimensionality boundary for point designs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every \(n\)-point design in \([0,1]^d\) has maximum-norm fill distance \(h_n\ge\tfrac12 n^{-1/d}\). Therefore coverage-only certification of a Lipschitz error of order \(\varepsilon\) requires \(\Omega(\varepsilon^{-d})\) sites in the worst case.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any n-point cube design has fill distance at least one half n to the minus one over d.
knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Dependent Covering Lower Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fill Distance, Dispersion, and Star Discrepancy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes three standard design-quality statistics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(D_n=\{u_1,\ldots,u_n\}\subset[0,1]^d\), define \(h_n=\sup_x\min_i\|x-u_i\|_\infty\), \(\operatorname{disp}(D_n)=\sup\{\lambda(B):B\text{ is an axis-parallel box},\ B\cap D_n=\varnothing\}\), and \(D_n^*=\sup_{a\in[0,1]^d}|n^{-1}\sum_i\mathbf1_{[0,a)}(u_i)-\lambda([0,a))|\). These measure metric covering, largest empty-box volume, and anchored-box distributional error, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fill distance, dispersion, and star discrepancy measure metric covering, empty boxes, and anchored-box distributional error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The three statistics encode distinct coverage information and require valid conversions before substitution.
knowledge_statements.title: Fill Distance, Dispersion, and Star Discrepancy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supplies valid cube-specific conversions among coverage statistics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite \(D_n\subset[0,1]^d\), with axis-parallel boxes and the maximum norm, \[h_n^d\le \operatorname{disp}(D_n)\le 2^dD_n^*.\] Consequently, \(h_n\le2(D_n^*)^{1/d}\), and either vanishing dispersion or vanishing star discrepancy implies vanishing fill distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the unit cube, fill distance is controlled through empty-box dispersion, which is in turn controlled by star discrepancy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_n^d\le\operatorname{disp}(D_n)\le2^dD_n^*\).
knowledge_statements.title: Valid Discrepancy-to-Covering Comparisons

assumptions_latex: The domain is \(X=[0,1]^d\), equipped with the maximum norm.
The evaluation design after \(n\) samples is \(D_n\subset X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The deterministic error certificate is \(0\le\min_{z\in D_n}f(z)-f^\star\le Lh_n\); thus any regime with \(h_n\to0\) is globally consistent.

notation.meaning: Volume of the largest empty axis-parallel box

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage measures as deterministic regimes controlling global-search error for Lipschitz objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_n\) be the first \(n\) evaluation sites. Its covering regime is described by \(h_n\), while its axis-parallel dispersion is the largest empty-box volume \(v_n\). A design is coverage-consistent when \(h_n\to0\); a rate \(h_n=O(a_n)\) defines an \(a_n\)-coverage regime. If \(x^\star\) minimizes \(f\), choose \(z_n\in D_n\) with \(\lVert z_n-x^\star\rVert_\infty\le h_n\). Lipschitz continuity then gives \(0\le\min_{z\in D_n}f(z)-f^\star\le Lh_n\). Consequently, coverage radius directly determines a worst-case optimization-error regime, whereas discrepancy or dispersion requires a geometric conversion before implying such a bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Covering radius directly bounds Lipschitz optimization error; discrepancy or empty-box volume affects optimization only after conversion to a covering guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Coverage Discrepancy Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited. The central mathematical claim is an explicit optimization-error certificate, so generic property is not the best exact kind; certificate is more appropriate. The relation between empty-box dispersion or discrepancy and covering radius is left unspecified, and the statement contains proof text.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected Builder claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The proposed universal inequality \(\operatorname{disp}(D_n)\le(2h_n)^d\) is false: an empty axis-parallel box may be highly elongated, so its volume is not controlled by the \(d\)-th power of its shortest scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dispersion is not universally bounded by (2h) to the d; elongated empty boxes invalidate that direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Builder's claimed two-sided comparison between \(h_n^d\) and dispersion cannot be accepted.
knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Reverse Dispersion Bound

intermediate_metadata.reason: This regime leaf owns definitions, valid conversions, the deferred Lipschitz-error regime, and dimensional covering limits. The Builder's false reverse dispersion bound is deferred. Quasirandom construction, randomized maximin coverage, and stratified sampling are excluded as sibling method scopes.

children.title: Transition-Population Search Family
children.top_down_role: Randomized global methods based on transitions or generations.

children.title: Markovian Global Search
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for stochastic transition-based search families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Markov condition for a stochastic global-search state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A state process \((X_n)\) is Markov with kernels \(K_n\) when, for every measurable \(A\), \[\mathbb P(X_{n+1}\in A\mid X_0,\ldots,X_n)=K_n(X_n,A)\quad\text{a.s.}\] Every archive, temperature, or adaptive parameter affecting the next transition must be included in \(X_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The current state must contain all transition-relevant information for the search to be Markov.
assumptions_latex: \((X_n)\) takes values in a measurable state space.
The conditional transition laws are represented by kernels \(K_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed conditional-law equality characterizes transition sufficiency of the declared Markov state.
knowledge_statements.title: Transition-State Sufficiency

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationarity Does Not Imply Global Optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between equilibrium and best-so-far optimization convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Existence of, or convergence to, an invariant distribution \(\pi\) does not by itself imply that \(X_n\) or \(\min_{i\le n}f(X_i)\) approaches a global minimum. If \(\pi(A_\varepsilon)=0\) for \(A_\varepsilon=\{x:f(x)<f^\star+\varepsilon\}\), a stationary chain has probability zero of occupying \(A_\varepsilon\) at any fixed time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equilibrium convergence is not an optimization guarantee without continued access to near-optimal regions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Invariant-distribution convergence alone is insufficient for global-search convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Does Not Imply Global Optimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Miss-probability bound under persistent conditional access to a measurable target set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let A be measurable and \tau_A=\inf\{n\ge1:X_n\in A\}. If, for n=0,\ldots,T-1, \Pr(X_{n+1}\in A\mid\mathcal F_n)\ge p_n almost surely on \{\tau_A>n\}, then \Pr(\tau_A>T)\le\prod_{n=0}^{T-1}(1-p_n)\le\exp(-\sum_{n=0}^{T-1}p_n).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional lower bounds on reaching a target set give product and exponential bounds on the probability of missing it through a finite horizon.
assumptions_latex: The displayed conditional lower bounds hold before the first hit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr(\tau_A>T)\le\prod_{n<T}(1-p_n)\le e^{-\sum_{n<T}p_n}.

notation.meaning: first positive-time visit to the target set
conditional lower bound on the next-step hit probability

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Horizon Conditional Hitting Bound

assumptions_latex: The feasible state space \(X\) is measurable and the objective \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is measurable.
For each incumbent level, the transition kernels assign uniformly persistent probability to every better sublevel set.
The algorithm records the best state visited.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the persistent-hitting condition, the recorded best value converges almost surely to \(f^\star=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\).

notation.meaning: Best objective value through time n

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-homogeneous or inhomogeneous Markov transitions with best-so-far recording.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(X_0\in X\). Given \(X_n=x\), draw \(X_{n+1}\) from \(K_n(x,\cdot)\), evaluate \(f(X_{n+1})\), and update \(B_{n+1}=\min\{B_n,f(X_{n+1})\}\). For every \(\varepsilon>0\), let \(A_\varepsilon=\{x:f(x)<f^\star+\varepsilon\}\). A sufficient global-search condition is the existence of numbers \(p_{n,\varepsilon}\in[0,1]\) satisfying \(K_n(x,A_\varepsilon)\ge p_{n,\varepsilon}\) for all \(x\), with \(\sum_n p_{n,\varepsilon}=\infty\). Then the chain hits each \(A_\varepsilon\) almost surely, and the recorded values converge to \(f^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Move through the domain using stochastic transition kernels and record the best state; persistent probability of hitting every near-optimal set ensures global convergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Markovian Global Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The kernel minorization and divergent-sum hitting claim requires an authoritative theorem-level source and precise filtration or conditional formulation. None is provided, and the statement includes inferential proof text. The algorithm kind fits the Markovian search container.

children.title: Simulated Annealing
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for temperature-controlled Markovian global search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state barrier example showing failure under summable uphill acceptance probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the path graph \(a-b-c\), with proposals moving to adjacent vertices, \(f(a)=0\), \(f(b)=H>0\), \(f(c)=-1\), and \(X_0=a\). If \(\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\exp(-H/T_n)<\infty\), then \(\Pr(X_n=a\text{ for every }n)>0\). Thus simulated annealing can remain forever at the nonglobal local minimum \(a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the probabilities of crossing a necessary energy barrier are summable, simulated annealing can remain in a nonglobal well with positive probability.
assumptions_latex: The proposal graph is the path \(a-b-c\), with positive adjacent-edge proposals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr(X_n=a\text{ for all }n)>0.\)

notation.meaning: energy barrier separating the initial well from the global minimum

knowledge_statements.title: Premature-Cooling Trap

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state symmetric-proposal Metropolis kernel underlying simulated annealing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite, let \(Q(x,y)=Q(y,x)\) be an irreducible proposal kernel, and fix \(T>0\). For \(y\ne x\), set \(P_T(x,y)=Q(x,y)\min\{1,\exp(-(f(y)-f(x))/T)\}\), with the diagonal chosen to make \(P_T\) stochastic. Then \(P_T\) is reversible with respect to \(\pi_T(x)=Z_T^{-1}\exp(-f(x)/T)\). Consequently \(\pi_T\) is its unique stationary distribution and \(\pi_T(X^\star)\to1\) as \(T\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At fixed temperature, finite-state Metropolis search with a symmetric irreducible proposal has a Gibbs stationary law that concentrates on global minimizers as temperature vanishes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_T(x)\propto e^{-f(x)/T}\) is the unique stationary distribution and \(\pi_T(X^\star)\to1\) as \(T\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Temperature Gibbs Reversibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state symmetric Metropolis annealing with a barrier-depth cooling threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite and let the symmetric proposal kernel induce a connected graph. Define \(H(\gamma)=\max_{z\in\gamma}f(z)\), \(H(x,A)=\min_{\gamma:x\leadsto A}H(\gamma)\), and \(\Gamma^\star=\max_{x\notin X^\star}(H(x,X^\star)-f(x))\). For the time-inhomogeneous Metropolis chain with \(T_n=c/\log(n+n_0)\), if \(c>\Gamma^\star\) and \(n_0>1\), then \(\Pr(X_n\in X^\star)\to1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite connected landscape, logarithmic cooling slower than the deepest nonglobal energy barrier yields convergence in probability to the global-minimizer set.
assumptions_latex: The symmetric proposal kernel is irreducible and assigns positive probability to every graph edge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{n\to\infty}\Pr(X_n\in X^\star)=1.\)

notation.meaning: minimum path elevation from a state to a set
maximum depth of a nonglobal energy well

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-State Logarithmic Cooling Theorem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-state annealing iteration allowing asymmetric proposals; symmetric Metropolis annealing is the special case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite, let \(T_n>0\), and let \(Q\) be an irreducible proposal kernel with mutual support: \(Q(x,y)>0\iff Q(y,x)>0\). Given \(X_n=x\), draw \(Y_n\sim Q(x,\cdot)\) and, when \(Q(x,Y_n)>0\), accept \(Y_n=y\) with probability \[\alpha_n(x,y)=\min\left\{1,\exp\left(-\frac{f(y)-f(x)}{T_n}\right)\frac{Q(y,x)}{Q(x,y)}\right\};\] otherwise retain \(x\). Record a least-objective incumbent among visited states. For symmetric \(Q\), the proposal ratio cancels. This definition makes no convergence claim for an arbitrary cooling schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-state simulated annealing uses temperature-dependent Metropolis-Hastings moves and records the best visited state.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is irreducible and has mutual support.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed rule defines finite-state simulated annealing and reduces to ordinary Metropolis annealing for symmetric \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.title: Metropolis-Hastings Simulated Annealing

assumptions_latex: The proposal kernel \(Q(x,\cdot)\) is irreducible on the feasible state space \(X\).
The positive temperature sequence \((T_n)\) decreases toward zero according to a schedule satisfying an appropriate global-convergence condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under a valid cooling condition, the probability of occupying any fixed nonoptimal energy level tends to zero, and best-so-far values approach the global minimum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metropolis simulated annealing; the precise sufficient cooling schedule depends on state-space assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(X_0\in X\) and temperatures \(T_n\downarrow0\). Given \(X_n=x\), propose \(Y_n\sim Q(x,\cdot)\) and accept it with probability \(\alpha_n(x,Y_n)=\min\{1,\exp(-(f(Y_n)-f(x))/T_n)\}\); otherwise set \(X_{n+1}=x\). Record the best state visited and stop according to a prescribed evaluation budget or convergence diagnostic. At fixed \(T\), the acceptance rule favors low objective values while allowing uphill moves. Global convergence requires sufficiently slow cooling relative to the energy barriers and irreducibility properties of the chosen state-space model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use Metropolis moves whose willingness to accept objective increases decreases with temperature; sufficiently slow cooling can concentrate the search on global minima.
knowledge_statements.title: Simulated Annealing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied, and an unspecified 'appropriate global-convergence condition' cannot support the stated concentration conclusion. Cooling theorems differ materially between finite, countable, and continuous state spaces; proposal irreducibility alone is insufficient. The algorithm kind fits, but the theorem component needs a precise sourced variant.

children.title: Population Evolution Search Family
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for population-based stochastic search families.

children.title: Generational Population Search
children.top_down_role: Population methods organized through successive generations of candidate points.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluation accounting for fixed-size synchronous offspring generations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If initialization evaluates \(N\) individuals and each of \(T\) generations evaluates exactly \(N\) new offspring without reevaluating retained individuals, the total number of evaluations is \(N(T+1)\). More generally, if generation \(t\) evaluates \(e_t\le N\) offspring, the total is \(N+\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}e_t\le N(T+1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full fixed-size generational method performs N(T+1) evaluations, with the displayed upper bound for partial offspring evaluation.
assumptions_latex: The initial population has size \(N\) and is evaluated once.
Retained unchanged individuals are not reevaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated exact count and upper bound hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Per-Generation Evaluation Count

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generational Replacement Is Not Necessarily Elitist
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes synchronous replacement from elite preservation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under pure replacement \(P_{t+1}=O_t\), the current best value can increase because a best member of \(P_t\) need not occur in \(O_t\). Monotonicity of the current-population minimum therefore requires elitist survival or an external archive; it does not follow from generational organization alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Whole-population replacement can lose the current best individual, so synchronous generations do not imply elitism.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Current-population best values need not be nonincreasing.
knowledge_statements.title: Generational Replacement Is Not Necessarily Elitist

assumptions_latex: The population size is a fixed integer \(N\ge1\).
Selection and variation define probability kernels on the population space \(X^N\).
Every generated individual is evaluated by the objective \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update defines a Markov chain on \(X^N\), and elitist survival makes the recorded best objective value nonincreasing across generations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous population replacement with optional elitism and a fixed evaluation budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(P_0\in X^N\) and evaluate all members. At generation \(t\), sample parents \(M_t\) from a selection kernel depending on the evaluated population, generate \(N\) offspring \(O_t\) through a variation kernel, and evaluate them. A generational replacement rule sets \(P_{t+1}=O_t\); an elitist rule instead applies a survivor kernel to \(P_t\cup O_t\) while retaining at least one current best individual. Stop after a prescribed number of generations or evaluations and output the best individual ever evaluated. Conditional on \(P_t\), the selection, variation, and replacement kernels determine the distribution of \(P_{t+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select parents, generate and evaluate an entire offspring population, then replace the current generation; elitism preserves the best value found.
knowledge_statements.title: Generational Population Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source or locator is supplied. The update is Markov on the population alone only when the kernels depend on no additional history or adaptive state, and the exact generational versus elitist replacement convention needs sourcing. The algorithm kind fits the terminal container.

children.title: Evolutionary Search
children.top_down_role: Global-search families based on evolutionary variation and selection.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation between retention and global reachability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Elitist survival preserves the best evaluated value but does not ensure discovery of better points. If a strict suboptimal class of population states is closed under selection, variation, and survival, a search initialized in that class cannot reach a global minimizer outside it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elite preservation cannot overcome a variation mechanism trapped in a suboptimal population class.
assumptions_latex: A strict suboptimal set of population states is closed under the selection, variation, and survival kernels.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Initialization in that closed class prevents global convergence to minimizers outside it.
knowledge_statements.title: Elitism Without Exploration Can Stagnate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise consequence of retaining evaluated best candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(b_t=\min\{f(x):x\text{ has been evaluated through iteration }t\}\). Then \(b_{t+1}\le b_t\). If survival retains a candidate attaining the current population minimum, then \(\min_{x\in P_{t+1}}f(x)\le\min_{x\in P_t}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An archive is always monotone, while monotonicity of the current population requires elitist survival.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
All compared candidates have been evaluated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Archived best values are nonincreasing; current-population best values are nonincreasing under elitist survival.

notation.meaning: Best objective value evaluated through iteration t

knowledge_statements.title: Elitist Best-So-Far Monotonicity

assumptions_latex: Candidate solutions lie in a measurable search space \(X\).
Selection, recombination, mutation, and survival are specified as stochastic kernels.
The objective \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) supplies the fitness ordering for minimization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure produces a stochastic population process whose best-so-far member is the reported approximate global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General evolutionary search template encompassing generational and steady-state replacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize and evaluate a finite population \(P_0\). At iteration \(t\), sample one or more parents with probabilities determined by a selection rule, apply recombination kernel \(C\) and mutation kernel \(M\) to obtain offspring, evaluate the offspring, and form \(P_{t+1}\) using a specified survival rule. The survival rule may replace the whole population or only selected members and may preserve elites. Continue until an evaluation budget or stated stopping predicate is met, then output \(x_{\mathrm{best}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{f(x):x\text{ was evaluated}\}\). Global-convergence claims additionally require an exploration condition ensuring continued access to every relevant region of \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iterate fitness-based selection, recombination, mutation, evaluation, and survival, returning the best candidate ever evaluated; convergence needs persistent global exploration.
knowledge_statements.title: Evolutionary Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied for this broad evolutionary-search template or its claimed scope across generational and steady-state variants. The global-exploration condition is mentioned but not stated mathematically. The algorithm kind fits, but the exact leaf sense and convergence qualification require a source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic conditional-hitting theorem proposed for evolutionary search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If, conditional on every history, iteration \(t\) evaluates a point in each measurable near-optimal set \(A_\varepsilon\) with probability at least \(p_{t,\varepsilon}\), where \(\sum_t p_{t,\varepsilon}=\infty\), then archived best values converge almost surely to the global infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divergent cumulative conditional probability of hitting every near-optimal set forces best-so-far convergence.
assumptions_latex: The objective and near-optimal sets are measurable.
The algorithm records its best evaluated value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The archived best value converges almost surely to the global infimum.

notation.meaning: Conditional lower bound on a near-optimal hit

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent-Mutation Global Convergence

intermediate_metadata.reason: Accepted local inventory: archive and elitist monotonicity plus the suboptimal-closed-class failure boundary. The proposed persistent-mutation theorem is deferred from this leaf because its canonical home is the generic almost-sure convergence topic. The deferred core evolutionary template leaves definitions and algorithms incomplete. Synchronous generations, diversity mechanisms, and selection-pressure regimes remain in sibling scopes.

children.title: Population Diversity Control
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms preserving exploratory variation within a search population.
