knowledge_statements.scope_note: A checkable survivor operator enforcing minimum metric separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Order a finite evaluated candidate pool by nondecreasing objective value with deterministic tie breaking. Scan in that order and accept \(x\) only if \(\rho(x,z)>r\) for every previously accepted survivor \(z\), stopping at the survivor capacity. The accepted set is pairwise more than \(r\) apart and contains the best-ranked candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedy survivor selection retains the best candidate and rejects later candidates lying within a chosen radius of an accepted survivor.
assumptions_latex: The candidate pool is finite and totally ordered by fitness and tie breaking.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted survivors are pairwise separated by more than \(r\), and the first-ranked candidate is retained.
knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Distance-Separated Survivor Selection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Diversity Alone Does Not Ensure Global Exploration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates population spread from reachability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A positive within-population diversity statistic does not imply access to every region of \(X\). A transition can preserve pairwise separation while keeping all members in a strict suboptimal invariant subset \(S\subset X\). Hence diversity control alone implies neither irreducibility nor global convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A population can remain diverse inside a suboptimal invariant region, so diversity is not a substitute for global reachability.
assumptions_latex: A strict suboptimal subset \(S\) is closed under the population transition.
The diversity requirement is feasible within \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The diversity requirement can hold indefinitely without reaching a global minimizer outside \(S\).
knowledge_statements.title: Diversity Alone Does Not Ensure Global Exploration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinct metric-space summaries used by diversity controls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\) in \((X,\rho)\), define \[\delta_{\min}(P)=\min_{i<j}\rho(x_i,x_j),\quad \Delta(P)=\frac{2}{N(N-1)}\sum_{i<j}\rho(x_i,x_j),\quad R(P)=\max_i\rho(x_i,c(P)).\] These statistics are generally inequivalent; for example, duplicate points and one distant outlier can give \(\delta_{\min}(P)=0\) while \(R(P)\) is large.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum separation, mean pairwise distance, and radius measure different aspects of diversity and are not interchangeable.
assumptions_latex: The center rule \(c(P)\) is declared when radius is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed statistics are well-defined and generally inequivalent.
knowledge_statements.title: Common Population-Diversity Statistics

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Packing Feasibility of a Separation Threshold
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility test for a minimum-distance population constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a metric space (X,\rho) and r\ge0, define M_r(X)=\sup\{|S|:S\subseteq X,\ \rho(x,z)>r\text{ for all distinct }x,z\in S\}. A population of N members satisfying \delta_{\min}(P)>r exists if and only if N\le M_r(X). Consequently, no enforcement operator can guarantee such a population when N>M_r(X).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimum-separation threshold is feasible exactly when the domain's packing number at that radius is at least the requested population size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists P\in X^N:\delta_{\min}(P)>r\iff N\le M_r(X).

notation.meaning: maximum attainable cardinality of an r-separated subset

knowledge_statements.title: Packing Feasibility of a Separation Threshold

assumptions_latex: The population is \(P=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\in X^N\) in a metric space \((X,\rho)\).
A diversity statistic and admissible range are fixed before the update.
The control operator can reject, repair, or replace candidates without altering already recorded evaluations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted population satisfies the prescribed diversity constraint, while any elitist implementation can simultaneously retain a best-so-far individual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A checkable pairwise-distance diversity constraint with rejection or repair enforcement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(N\ge2\), define the mean pairwise diversity \(\Delta(P)=\frac{2}{N(N-1)}\sum_{1\le i<j\le N}\rho(x_i,x_j)\). At iteration \(t\), a population satisfies the diversity-control condition when \(\Delta(P_t)\ge\delta_t\), where \(\delta_t\) is a prescribed nonnegative threshold. Given a proposed population \(P'_t\), accept it only if the condition holds; otherwise apply a specified repair or replacement operator until the inequality holds or a declared failure limit is reached. An elitist repair must retain at least one member attaining the best objective value previously recorded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Require population mean pairwise distance to exceed a chosen threshold, repairing or rejecting populations that violate it while optionally preserving an elite.
knowledge_statements.title: Population Diversity Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is cited. A prescribed threshold can be infeasible for the metric space and population size, so repair need not produce an accepted population; the conclusion needs an explicit feasibility or conditional-success hypothesis. The record also mixes a diversity condition with an enforcement algorithm, making the selected condition kind only partially aligned.

children.title: Selection-Pressure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Behavior associated with weak, balanced, or aggressive population selection.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Premature-convergence boundary when nonbest parents receive zero probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If selection assigns zero probability to every nonbest candidate and variation from current best candidates is confined to a strict reachable subset, then a global minimizer outside that subset has zero discovery probability. Increasing selection pressure is therefore not necessarily a monotone improvement in global-search reliability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Selecting only current best candidates can eliminate material needed to reach better basins when variation lacks independent global support.
assumptions_latex: Nonbest candidates receive zero parent-selection probability.
Variation from current best candidates is confined to a strict reachable subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A global minimizer outside that subset cannot be discovered.
knowledge_statements.title: Maximal Pressure Can Destroy Exploration

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rank Pressure Is Invariant to Objective-Gap Magnitude
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes rank-based from magnitude-sensitive selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed ranks, tournament-selection probabilities are unchanged by any strictly increasing transformation of objective values. Thus tournament pressure cannot distinguish populations with identical rankings but different objective gaps, whereas magnitude-based rules generally can.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tournament selection responds to ranks, not to the sizes of objective gaps.
assumptions_latex: The transformation preserves the candidates' total rank order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Tournament-selection probabilities are unchanged when only objective-gap magnitudes change.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank Pressure Is Invariant to Objective-Gap Magnitude

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rank-based pressure parameterization for tournaments sampled with replacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Rank \(N\) candidates from best to worst. Draw \(k\ge1\) ranks independently and uniformly with replacement and select the best sampled rank. Then \[p_r(k)=\left(\frac{N-r+1}{N}\right)^k-\left(\frac{N-r}{N}\right)^k.\] Thus \(k=1\) is uniform selection, while the best-rank probability \(1-(1-1/N)^k\) increases with \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tournament size parameterizes rank pressure: size one is uniform, and larger tournaments increasingly favor better ranks.
assumptions_latex: \(N\ge1\) candidates have a deterministic total rank order.
Tournament draws are independent, uniform, and with replacement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed formula gives the rank-selection probabilities, and the best-rank probability is nondecreasing in \(k\).
knowledge_statements.title: Tournament-Selection Pressure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-independent comparison of rank-based parent-selection pressure; informal regime labels still require a declared family or threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Rank \(N\) candidates from best to worst, and let \(p_r^A\) and \(p_r^B\) be their parent-selection probabilities under rules \(A\) and \(B\). Rule \(A\) has at least as much rank-selection pressure as \(B\) when \[\sum_{r=1}^{m}p_r^A\geq\sum_{r=1}^{m}p_r^B\qquad(m=1,\ldots,N).\] Dominance is strict if at least one inequality is strict. Uniform rank selection is a neutral reference, deterministic selection of rank one is maximal in this order, and rules unrelated by these inequalities have incomparable rank-pressure profiles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-based rule exerts greater selection pressure when it assigns at least as much probability to every top-ranked prefix.
assumptions_latex: The population has \(N\geq1\) candidates with a deterministic total rank order.
Each rule defines a probability distribution over ranks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cumulative-prefix inequalities define a partial order of rank-selection pressure; best-only selection is maximal, while some rules are incomparable.

notation.meaning: Probability that rule A selects rank r

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Distribution Ordering of Selection Pressure

assumptions_latex: A population contains candidates with finite objective values \(f_1,ldots,f_N\).
Parent selection uses Boltzmann weights with inverse-selection parameter \(\beta\ge0\).
All candidates with finite objective values receive positive selection probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(\beta=0\) selection is uniform; finite \(\beta>0\) gives soft selection; and \(\beta\to\infty\) concentrates probability on the current minimizers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boltzmann selection provides a precise weak-to-strong pressure parameterization for minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For objective values \(f_1,ldots,f_N\), define \(p_i(\beta)=\exp(-\beta f_i)/\sum_{j=1}^N\exp(-\beta f_j)\). The selection-pressure ratio between candidates \(i\) and \(j\) is \(p_i(\beta)/p_j(\beta)=\exp(\beta(f_j-f_i))\). The regime \(\beta=0\) is neutral selection, since \(p_i(0)=1/N\). Finite \(\beta>0\) is soft fitness-biased selection, with every candidate retaining positive probability. As \(\beta\to\infty\), total probability concentrates uniformly on the indices attaining \(\min_j f_j\), defining the limiting maximal-pressure regime. Thus increasing \(\beta\) monotonically amplifies every fixed favorable objective gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boltzmann selection ranges from uniform sampling at zero pressure to concentration on current best candidates as inverse temperature grows.
knowledge_statements.title: Selection-Pressure Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied for choosing Boltzmann selection as the representation of this regime leaf. Both the assumptions and statement contain malformed LaTeX, writing `ldots` instead of \(\ldots\). Because the record parameterizes and characterizes regimes rather than imposing a condition, representation or property is a better exact kind than condition.

children.title: Statistical-Model-Based Search
children.top_down_role: Global search guided by stochastic-process, random-field, or response-surface models.

children.title: Random-Process Models
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for process-based statistical search models.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: An Incomplete Search State Need Not Be Markov
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-sufficiency boundary for adaptive process models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a next-step rule uses transition-relevant information not measurable with respect to the declared current state, then the declared state process need not be Markov. Including all such information in an augmented state restores the Markov representation when the conditional laws are kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A search state is Markov only when it contains every history variable used by the transition rule.
assumptions_latex: At least one transition-relevant history variable is absent from the declared state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The declared state can fail to be Markov, while a transition-sufficient augmented state is Markov.
knowledge_statements.title: An Incomplete Search State Need Not Be Markov

knowledge_statements.scope_note: State augmentation for a history-dependent discrete-time search process.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the next-step law of \(S_{n+1}\) be a probability kernel \(Q_n(\cdot\mid H_n)\) depending on \(H_n=(S_0,\ldots,S_n)\). Defining \(Z_n=H_n\) yields a Markov process whose transition kernel appends a draw from \(Q_n(\cdot\mid Z_n)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A history-dependent search becomes Markov after its state is augmented with all transition-relevant history.
assumptions_latex: Search variables and finite histories have measurable state spaces.
Each next-step conditional law is represented by a probability kernel.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented history process \((Z_n)\) is Markov.

notation.meaning: Complete search history through iteration n

knowledge_statements.title: History-State Markovization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Kernel Construction of a Discrete-Time Search Process
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence and uniqueness in law from an initial distribution and history-dependent transition kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let (S,\mathcal S) be a measurable space, let \mu_0 be a probability measure on it, and for each n\ge0 let Q_n(\cdot\mid s_0,\ldots,s_n) be a probability kernel from (S^{n+1},\mathcal S^{\otimes(n+1)}) to (S,\mathcal S). Then there is a unique probability measure on (S^{\mathbb N_0},\mathcal S^{\otimes\mathbb N_0}) whose initial law is \mu_0 and whose successive conditional laws are Q_n.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An initial law and measurable history-dependent kernels uniquely determine the law of a discrete-time search process.
assumptions_latex: (S,\mathcal S) is a measurable state space.
\mu_0 is a probability measure on (S,\mathcal S).
Each Q_n is a probability kernel on the declared finite-history space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{A unique path-space probability law realizes the specified process}.
knowledge_statements.title: Kernel Construction of a Discrete-Time Search Process

assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty and \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) is the objective.
\((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) carries an increasing filtration \((\mathcal F_n)_{n\geq 0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The process model specifies the conditional law used to generate and assess the next search state.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-time stochastic-process model for adaptive global search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A random-process search model is an adapted stochastic process \((Z_n)_{n\geq 0}\), where \(Z_n\) contains the sampled points, observed objective values, and incumbent after iteration \(n\). Its evolution is specified by probability kernels \(K_n\) satisfying \[\mathbb P(Z_{n+1}\in A\mid\mathcal F_n)=K_n(Z_n,A)\] for every measurable state set \(A\). The kernel may depend on all accumulated information, so the model includes independent random search, history-dependent sampling, and stochastic transitions followed by local optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random-process model represents global search as an adapted sequence whose conditional transition law may depend on all observations and incumbents collected so far.
knowledge_statements.title: Random-Process Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the process-model container, but no citation is supplied. The measurable state space of Z_n is not specified, and K_n(Z_n,A) is Markov in the stated state even though the prose says the kernel may depend on all accumulated information; a source and a precise state/history formulation are required.

children.title: Random-Field Models
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for spatial statistical models of global objectives.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity of a Second-Order Random-Field Kernel
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient covariance-kernel condition for a real second-order field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symmetric function \(k:D\times D\to\mathbb R\) is the covariance kernel of a real second-order random field indexed by \(D\) if and only if, for every \(n\ge1\), \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\in D\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \[\sum_{i,j=1}^n c_i c_j k(x_i,x_j)\ge0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetric function is a valid covariance kernel exactly when every finite Gram matrix is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k\) is a covariance kernel if and only if all its finite Gram matrices are positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.title: Validity of a Second-Order Random-Field Kernel

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mean and Covariance Do Not Determine a General Field
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiability boundary between Gaussian and general second-order fields.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two second-order random fields can have identical mean and covariance functions but different finite-dimensional distributions. Thus \((m,k)\) alone need not determine a field law or its conditional laws; it does determine a Gaussian field law.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mean and covariance determine a Gaussian field but generally do not determine a non-Gaussian field or its posterior.
assumptions_latex: The compared fields have finite second moments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality of first and second moments need not imply equality of field laws outside an identifying family such as the Gaussian family.
knowledge_statements.title: Mean and Covariance Do Not Determine a General Field

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise conditional law under independent Gaussian observation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a Gaussian field with mean \(m\) and covariance \(k\). For \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), let \(y=F_X+\varepsilon\), where \(\varepsilon\sim N(0,\Sigma)\) is independent of \(F\). If \(K+\Sigma\) is nonsingular, then \[F(x)\mid y\sim N\!\left(m(x)+k_X(x)^\top(K+\Sigma)^{-1}(y-m_X),\ k(x,x)-k_X(x)^\top(K+\Sigma)^{-1}k_X(x)\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gaussian-field conditioning gives explicit posterior means and variances from the covariance and noise matrices.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is Gaussian with mean \(m\) and covariance \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed normal distribution is the conditional pointwise law of \(F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Dimensional Gaussian-Field Conditioning

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translation-invariant spatial dependence for a second-order real random field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A second-order field on D\subseteq\mathbb R^d is weakly stationary when \mathbb E[F(x)]=\mu and \operatorname{Cov}(F(x),F(x+h))=C(h) whenever both sites lie in D. Its semivariogram satisfies \gamma(h)=\tfrac12\mathbb E[(F(x+h)-F(x))^2]=C(0)-C(h). Isotropy imposes the additional restriction C(h)=c(\|h\|).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a weakly stationary field, covariance depends only on displacement and the semivariogram equals covariance loss from zero lag; isotropy additionally removes directional dependence.
assumptions_latex: Both x and x+h belong to D.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \gamma(h)=C(0)-C(h),\qquad C(h)=c(\|h\|)\text{ under isotropy}.

notation.meaning: stationary covariance function at displacement h

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Stationarity and Variogram Relation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Dimensional Laws Determine a Random Field
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Law-level characterization of a real-valued random field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an index set D, the law of F=(F(x))_{x\in D} on (\mathbb R^D,\mathcal C), where \mathcal C is the cylinder \sigma-algebra, is uniquely determined by all finite-dimensional distributions \mathcal L(F(x_1),\ldots,F(x_n)). Conversely, every projectively consistent family of such finite-dimensional probability laws defines a unique field law on \mathcal C.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random-field law is exactly encoded by a projectively consistent collection of finite-dimensional distributions.
assumptions_latex: The finite-dimensional laws are permutation-compatible and consistent under marginalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{There is a unique law on }(\mathbb R^D,\mathcal C)\text{ with the prescribed finite-dimensional distributions}.

notation.meaning: cylinder sigma-algebra on the coordinate space

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Dimensional Laws Determine a Random Field

assumptions_latex: The objective is observed at finitely many sampled locations, possibly with noise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Conditioning the field on observations yields a spatial surrogate distribution over objective values on \(D\).

notation.meaning: Random field indexed by the decision point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spatial stochastic surrogate for an unknown continuous objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A random-field model for an objective on \(D\) is a collection \(\{F(x):x\in D\}\) of jointly distributed random variables. In a second-order model, \[m(x)=\mathbb E[F(x)],\qquad k(x,x')=\operatorname{Cov}(F(x),F(x'))\] specify its mean and spatial dependence. Given observations \(Y_i=F(x_i)+\varepsilon_i\), conditioning on \(\{(x_i,Y_i)\}_{i=1}^n\) produces a posterior or conditional field whose pointwise distributions quantify predicted objective values and uncertainty throughout \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random-field model assigns jointly distributed objective values across the domain and conditions that spatial model on sampled, possibly noisy observations.
knowledge_statements.title: Random-Field Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record has the correct definitional role and local spatial sense, but it has no source. The observation errors epsilon_i and their joint relationship with the field are not introduced, so the claimed conditional field is not mathematically determined without additional modeling assumptions.

children.title: Surrogate Global-Search Interface
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for modern surrogate-search ownership outside this chapter.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-defined candidate request when an acquisition supremum need not be attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty \(D\), an acquisition function \(a_n:D\to\mathbb R\) bounded above, and \(\eta_n>0\), an admissible response is any \(x_{n+1}\in D\) satisfying \[a_n(x_{n+1})\ge\sup_{x\in D}a_n(x)-\eta_n.\] Exact maximization may instead be requested when the supremum is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface can request an approximately acquisition-maximizing point without assuming that an exact maximizer exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At least one admissible approximate response exists by the definition of the supremum.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Acquisition-Selection Contract

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Surrogate Merit Is Not a Global Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certification boundary for model-guided black-box search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A surrogate prediction, posterior variance, acquisition value, or failure to improve observed values does not by itself establish \(f(x_{\mathrm{inc}})-\inf_{x\in D}f(x)\le\varepsilon\). Such a conclusion requires a valid domain-wide error bound or lower-bound argument linking the surrogate to the true objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Surrogate scores and empirical stagnation do not certify global optimality without a rigorous domain-wide error or lower bound.
assumptions_latex: Only evaluated values and unvalidated surrogate outputs are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No finite global-optimality gap follows solely from those surrogate outputs.
knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate Merit Is Not a Global Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incumbent update from a finite evaluated point-value history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty finite evaluated history \mathcal D_n\subseteq D\times\mathbb R, define v_n=\min\{y:(x,y)\in\mathcal D_n\} and I(\mathcal D_n)=\{x\in D:(x,v_n)\in\mathcal D_n\}. An incumbent update selects x_n^{\mathrm{inc}}\in I(\mathcal D_n); the incumbent is a point, while v_n is its recorded value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The incumbent is selected from the point projection of the best-valued data pairs, rather than being assigned an entire point-value pair.
assumptions_latex: Every element of \mathcal D_n is an evaluated point-value pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I(\mathcal D_n)\ne\varnothing,\qquad x_n^{\mathrm{inc}}\in D.

notation.meaning: evaluated points attaining the best recorded value

knowledge_statements.title: Type-Correct Incumbent Projection

assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^d\) is the feasible domain and evaluations of \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\) are available.
At iteration \(n\), a surrogate distribution or predictor can be fitted from the evaluation history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface returns an evaluated candidate and updates the incumbent without requiring the global-search controller to know the surrogate's internal representation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-agnostic ask–evaluate–update interface for surrogate global search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with evaluated data \(\mathcal D_0=\{(x_i,f(x_i))\}_{i=1}^{n_0}\). At iteration \(n\), fit or update a surrogate from \(\mathcal D_n\), construct a measurable merit function \(a_n:D\to\mathbb R\), and request \[x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in D}a_n(x).\] Evaluate \(f(x_{n+1})\), set \(\mathcal D_{n+1}=\mathcal D_n\cup\{(x_{n+1},f(x_{n+1}))\}\), and update \(x_{n+1}^{\mathrm{inc}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,y)\in\mathcal D_{n+1}}y\). Stop under a prescribed evaluation budget or accuracy rule and return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The interface repeatedly fits a surrogate, asks it for a merit-maximizing candidate, evaluates that candidate, updates the data, and returns the best observation.
knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate Global-Search Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An algorithm is appropriate for this interface container, but the interface has no cited source. In addition, argmin over pairs (x,y) returns a pair rather than the point assigned to x_{n+1}^{inc}, and existence of an acquisition maximizer is not assumed or replaced by an approximate-selection rule.

children.title: Multistart Basin Search Family
children.top_down_role: Methods using repeated local optimization and basin identification.

children.title: Random Multistart
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for randomized initialization coupled to local solvers.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Multistart Is Not a Global Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates finite confidence from deterministic certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<p<1\), every finite run has positive miss probability \((1-p)^N\). Thus the best returned local minimizer and its local optimality conditions do not certify global optimality. A confidence claim requires a justified lower bound on \(p\), while deterministic certification requires an independent global bound or exhaustive argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite multistart is not a deterministic global certificate, and even probabilistic confidence requires a justified basin-mass bound.
assumptions_latex: Only finitely many independent starts are run.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent is not certified globally optimal by multistart alone.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Multistart Is Not a Global Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States when repeated starts do not imply eventual global discovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\mu(G)=0\), countably many independent starts hit \(G\) with probability zero. Positive marginal mass is also insufficient under arbitrary dependence: if \(X_n=X_1\) for every \(n\), eventual success probability is only \(\mu(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero-mass basins are never hit, and dependent repetition can defeat eventual success despite positive marginal basin mass.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is the set of starts whose local solves reach a global solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Neither \(\mu(G)=0\) nor arbitrary dependence supports almost-sure discovery.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Mass and Dependence Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact success law for independent starts followed by a fixed local solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=\{x\in D:L(x)\in M^\star\}\) be measurable and let \(p=\mu(G)\). For independent \(X_i\sim\mu\), \[\Pr\{\exists i\le N:L(X_i)\in M^\star\}=1-(1-p)^N.\] If \(0<p<1\), failure probability at most \(\alpha\) is ensured by \(N\ge\lceil\log(\alpha)/\log(1-p)\rceil\); if \(p>0\), eventual success has probability one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With global-basin mass p, N independent starts succeed with probability one minus (1-p) to the N.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr(\exists i\le N:L(X_i)\in M^\star)=1-(1-p)^N\).

notation.meaning: Union of globally minimizing attraction basins

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Sample Basin-Hit Probability

assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb R^d\) is measurable and \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is bounded below.
A local solver \(L\) maps each admissible start to a feasible local minimizer.
Starts are sampled independently from a probability measure \(\mu\) on \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned value is the best local minimum found from the sampled starts.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent random initialization followed by deterministic or stochastic local solution.

source_refs.locator: 2.1.2 Formal Scheme of Global Random Search Algorithms p. 33

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a run limit \(N\). For \(k=1,\ldots,N\), draw \(X_k\sim\mu\), compute \(Y_k=L(X_k)\), and update \[x_k^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\{Y_1,\ldots,Y_k\}}f(y).\] The algorithm stops after \(N\) local solves, or earlier under a prescribed budget or target-value rule, and outputs \(x_k^*\). If every neighborhood of every global minimizer has positive \(\mu\)-measure and such a neighborhood lies in its local basin, the probability of missing that basin after \(N\) starts tends to zero as \(N\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random multistart samples initial points, locally optimizes each one, and returns the best local solution; positive-measure global basins are eventually hit with probability one.
knowledge_statements.title: Random Multistart

source_witnesses.locator: 2.1.2 Formal Scheme of Global Random Search Algorithms p. 33

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite multistart algorithm is precise and appropriately classified, but the cited locator is the formal algorithm scheme on p. 33, while the record also asserts asymptotic basin-hitting convergence. That claim needs a supporting convergence locator, such as the separately inventoried Section 2.1.3 on p. 34, and full-text confirmation.

children.title: Clustering Multistart
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for basin identification and suppression of duplicate local searches.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local-Solver Basins and Exact Basin Labels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the objects identified by clustering multistart.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a deterministic local-solver map \(L:D\to M=L(D)\), the attraction basin of \(y\in M\) is \(B_y=L^{-1}(\{y\})\). The relation \(x\sim_L z\iff L(x)=L(z)\) is an equivalence relation whose nonempty classes are the basins. An exact basin label \(c\) satisfies \(c(x)=c(z)\iff L(x)=L(z)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic local solver partitions its starting domain into basins, and an exact basin label identifies starts having the same terminal solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) is partitioned by the nonempty sets \(B_y\).

notation.meaning: Attraction basin of terminal solution y

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Solver Basins and Exact Basin Labels

knowledge_statements.statement_title: False Basin Merging Can Lose the Global Basin
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safety boundary for geometric duplicate suppression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If one cluster contains \(x,z\) with \(L(x)\ne L(z)\), retaining only one representative can remove one attainable terminal solution. If \(L(z)\) is globally optimal but \(x\) is retained, suppression can lose the only sampled global-basin start. Geometric proximity alone therefore does not establish basin equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merging distinct true basins can suppress the only start leading to a global solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One-representative suppression need not preserve \(L(S)\) or a sampled global-basin hit.
knowledge_statements.title: False Basin Merging Can Lose the Global Basin

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes safe one-representative-per-cluster suppression on a finite candidate set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subset D\) be finite and suppose \(c(x)=c(z)\Rightarrow L(x)=L(z)\). Solving one representative from every nonempty cluster \(c^{-1}(i)\) returns exactly the set \(L(S)\). The reverse implication is unnecessary for safety; its failure only leaves redundant solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cluster suppression preserves every candidate outcome when no cluster merges starts with different local-solver outcomes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One solve per nonempty cluster recovers exactly \(L(S)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Safe Duplicate-Solve Suppression

assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb R^d\) is measurable and candidate starts are sampled from \(D\).
A local solver \(L\) and a clustering rule with radius or membership criterion are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local optimization is launched only from representatives not assigned to an already explored cluster or basin.

notation.meaning: Sampled candidate set at stage k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic clustering multistart scheme; cluster geometry is intentionally parameterized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\mathcal C_0=\varnothing\) and no incumbent. At stage \(k\), sample a finite set \(S_k\subset D\), rank its points by objective value, and assign each point to a cluster using the prescribed distance or connectivity rule. For each selected representative \(r\) not assigned to an explored cluster, compute \(y=L(r)\), record \(y\), and augment \(\mathcal C_k\) with the cluster associated with its attraction basin. Update the incumbent to the recorded point of smallest objective value. Stop at the sampling or local-solve budget and return that incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clustering multistart groups sampled points into prospective basins and launches local optimization only from representatives of basins not already explored.
knowledge_statements.title: Clustering Multistart

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the clustering-multistart container, but no source is supplied. The statement also moves from clusters defined by an arbitrary distance or connectivity rule to a cluster associated with an attraction basin without defining or justifying that correspondence.

children.title: Sequential Improvement of Local Minima
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for organized transitions among discovered local solutions.

assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb R^d\) is the feasible set and \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is bounded below.
A local solver returns a local minimizer from every accepted trial point.
A transition generator proposes points outside or beyond the current local basin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted transition produces a strictly decreasing sequence of recorded local-minimum values.

notation.meaning: Recorded local minimizer at stage k
Trial point generated from the current local minimizer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone transition scheme among locally minimized solutions.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.3 Sequential Improvement of Local Minima p. 27

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute an initial local minimizer \(x_0\). At stage \(k\), generate a trial point \(z_k\) by the prescribed basin-escape or global-sampling rule and compute \(y_k=L(z_k)\). Accept \(x_{k+1}=y_k\) only if \(f(y_k)<f(x_k)\); otherwise retain \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) or generate another trial. Thus every genuine transition satisfies \[f(x_{k+1})<f(x_k).\] Stop under a transition, evaluation, or stagnation rule and return the best recorded local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method escapes a discovered basin, locally minimizes from a trial point, and accepts a new local minimizer only when it strictly improves the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Improvement of Local Minima

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.3 Sequential Improvement of Local Minima p. 27

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary reachability condition and stagnation boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If all transition paths from the incumbent remain in a closed reachable class \(C\) of local minima satisfying \(\min_{y\in C}f(y)>f^\star\), sequential improvement cannot reach a global minimizer. Failure to generate an improving trial certifies globality only when the escape mechanism validly excludes every lower-valued feasible basin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed class of suboptimal local minima traps sequential improvement, and ordinary stagnation is not a global certificate.
assumptions_latex: The transition mechanism has a closed reachable class \(C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method cannot attain \(f^\star\) from that class.

notation.meaning: Closed reachable class of local minima

knowledge_statements.title: Unreachable Better Basin Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates convergence of accepted values from convergence or optimality of the states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) is bounded below and every accepted transition satisfies \(f(x_{k+1})<f(x_k)\), the accepted objective values converge to a finite \(\ell\ge\inf_D f\). This does not imply convergence of \((x_k)\), attainment of \(\ell\), or \(\ell=\min_D f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded strict descent guarantees convergence of accepted values only, not convergence of points or global optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_k)\downarrow\ell\ge\inf_D f\) along accepted states, with no stronger conclusion absent further assumptions.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone-Value Limit without State Convergence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination over Finitely Many Reachable Local Values
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accepted-transition bound for a finite reachable value set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=\{f(y):y\text{ is a reachable local minimizer}\}\) be finite. If every accepted state is a reachable local minimizer and every genuine transition strictly decreases its value, at most \(|V|-1\) transitions are accepted. The terminal state is optimal among reachable local minimizers exactly when no reachable local minimizer has a smaller value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With finitely many reachable local-minimum values, strict improvement accepts at most one fewer transitions than the number of such values.
assumptions_latex: Every accepted state is a reachable local minimizer.
Accepted transitions strictly decrease the objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At most \(|V|-1\) transitions are accepted.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Termination over Finitely Many Reachable Local Values

children.title: Certified Global–Local Hybrids
children.top_down_role: Architectures combining global bounds or exploration with local nonlinear improvement.

children.title: Incumbent Local Polishing
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for improving feasible global-search incumbents.

assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb R^d\) is the feasible set and \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is the objective.
A global-search method has produced a feasible incumbent \(x^{\mathrm{inc}}\).
A local solver can be initialized at feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Polishing preserves feasibility and never worsens the incumbent objective value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-preserving local improvement of a global-search incumbent.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.2 'Globalized' Local Optimization Strategies, Combined with Grid Search or Random Search p. 24

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a feasible incumbent \(x^{\mathrm{inc}}\), run the local solver from that point to obtain \(x^{\mathrm{loc}}=L(x^{\mathrm{inc}})\in D\). Update by \[x^+=\begin{cases}x^{\mathrm{loc}},&f(x^{\mathrm{loc}})<f(x^{\mathrm{inc}}),\\x^{\mathrm{inc}},&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\] The polishing call terminates according to the local solver's stationarity, step-size, or evaluation-budget rule. Its output \(x^+\) is feasible and satisfies \(f(x^+)\leq f(x^{\mathrm{inc}})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incumbent polishing starts a local solver from the best feasible global-search point and accepts the result only when it improves the objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Local Polishing

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.2 'Globalized' Local Optimization Strategies, Combined with Grid Search or Random Search p. 24

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Stationarity Is Not Global Certification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation between local incumbent improvement and proof of global quality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even if polishing returns a feasible point satisfying first- or second-order local optimality conditions, that point may be a nonglobal local minimizer. Therefore local solver termination, stationarity, or failure to find an improving step cannot justify global pruning or certify a global optimality gap without an independent valid global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polished stationary point can remain nonglobal, so polishing improves primal solutions but does not certify global quality or pruning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{local stationarity}\nRightarrow\text{global optimality or valid global pruning}.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Stationarity Is Not Global Certification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validated admission of a numerical local-solver candidate, already owned by a dedicated validation leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a certified incumbent \(x^{\mathrm{inc}}\), let a local solver propose \(\hat x\). Independently validate \(\hat x\in D\) and compare rigorous objective enclosures. Accept \(\hat x\) only when the enclosures certify strict improvement; otherwise retain \(x^{\mathrm{inc}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independently validate feasibility and objective improvement before admitting a numerical local-solver proposal as the new incumbent.
assumptions_latex: All feasibility and objective enclosures used for admission are rigorous.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^+\in D\quad\text{and, if accepted,}\quad f(x^+)<f(x^{\mathrm{inc}}).
knowledge_statements.title: Validated Safeguarded Polishing

intermediate_metadata.reason: The locally owned inventory is incumbent-started local refinement, feasibility-preserving monotone acceptance, and the sharp boundary that local stationarity is not global certification. The proposed validated-safeguard record was deferred because an existing dedicated leaf owns that mechanism. Global exploration and rigorous bound-gap certification remain in the two sibling scopes.

children.title: Globalized Local Search
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for local-search families augmented by global exploration.

assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb R^d\) is measurable, \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) is bounded below, and \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\geq 0}\) is the information filtration of the search.
A local-solver map \(L:D\to D\) and an \(\mathcal F_k\)-adapted incumbent sequence \((x_k^*)_{k\geq 0}\) are available.
There is a measurable attraction basin \(B\subset D\) of a global minimizer such that \(L(z)\) is globally minimizing for every \(z\in B\).
For some \(\delta>0\), the exploration trial \(z_k\) satisfies \(\mathbb P(z_k\in B\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq\delta\) almost surely for every \(k\geq1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The globalized local-search scheme reaches the global-minimizer basin with probability one and thereafter retains a globally minimizing incumbent.

notation.meaning: Information available before exploration step k
Global exploration trial at iteration k
Attraction basin of a global minimizer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure basin reachability for globalized local search under a uniform conditional exploration bound.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.2 'Globalized' Local Optimization Strategies, Combined with Grid Search or Random Search p. 24
2.1.3 Convergence of Global Random Search Algorithms p. 34

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), generate an exploration trial \(z_k\), compute \(y_k=L(z_k)\), and choose \[x_k^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\{x_{k-1}^*,y_k\}}f(x).\] If a measurable global-minimizer basin \(B\) satisfies \(\mathbb P(z_k\in B\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq\delta\) almost surely for a constant \(\delta>0\) and every \(k\geq1\), then \[\mathbb P(z_k\notin B\text{ for }k=1,\ldots,N)\leq(1-\delta)^N.\] Consequently, the search reaches \(B\) with probability one. Because \(L(z)\) is globally minimizing for \(z\in B\) and the update retains the better point, a globally minimizing incumbent is retained after the first such visit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every exploration step has a uniform positive conditional probability of entering a global-minimizer basin, globalized local search reaches that basin almost surely and then retains a global solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Globalized Local Search

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.2 'Globalized' Local Optimization Strategies, Combined with Grid Search or Random Search p. 24
2.1.3 Convergence of Global Random Search Algorithms p. 34

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonpersistent Exploration Gives No Global Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of basin reachability when global exploration may permanently miss the global basin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the local solver maps each start to a minimizer in its attraction basin. If there is positive probability that no exploration start ever enters a global-minimizer basin \(B\), then the method has positive probability of remaining at a nonglobal local minimizer. In particular, finitely many starts provide no general global-convergence guarantee. Local descent and best-so-far retention alone do not imply global convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without persistent coverage of a global basin, globalized local search can remain at a nonglobal local minimum.
assumptions_latex: The objective has a nonglobal local-minimizer basin and a disjoint global-minimizer basin \(B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb P(\forall k:\ z_k\notin B)>0\implies\mathbb P(\text{the global basin is never reached})>0.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonpersistent Exploration Gives No Global Guarantee

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dense Deterministic Starts Reach Open Global Basins
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic counterpart to probabilistic basin reachability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be a metric space, let \((z_k)\) have dense range in \(D\), and let \(B\subseteq D\) be a nonempty open attraction basin such that \(L(z)\) returns a global minimizer for every \(z\in B\). Then some \(z_k\in B\). If the incumbent update retains the best local-solver output, it retains a global minimizer after the first such index.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic start sequence with dense range eventually enters every nonempty open global basin and thereafter retains the resulting global minimizer.
assumptions_latex: The range \(\{z_k:k\ge1\}\) is dense in the metric search domain \(D\).
\(B\subseteq D\) is a nonempty open global-minimizer attraction basin.
\(L(z)\) is globally minimizing for every \(z\in B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists k:\ z_k\in B,\quad\text{and a best-so-far update thereafter retains a global minimizer}.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense Deterministic Starts Reach Open Global Basins

children.title: Heuristic Incumbents with Certified Bounds
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for noncertifying primal search paired with rigorous lower bounds.

assumptions_latex: \(D\) is a nonempty feasible set, \(f:D\to\mathbb R\), and the global optimal value \(f^*=\inf_{x\in D}f(x)\) is finite.
A heuristic supplies a feasible point \(\bar x\in D\), and a rigorous bounding method supplies \(L\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \(L\leq f^*\).
The requested absolute tolerance is \(\varepsilon\geq0\); for the scaled relative criterion, the declared scale satisfies \(s>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pair \((\bar x,L)\) certifies \(0\leq f(\bar x)-f^*\leq f(\bar x)-L\), and hence certifies the stated absolute or scaled relative tolerance when its computable gap satisfies the corresponding test.

notation.meaning: Declared positive scale for the relative criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute or scaled relative optimality-gap certificate for a heuristic incumbent.

source_refs.locator: 2.5 Local, Global, epsilon-Global Minima p. 57

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be a nonempty feasible set, let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\), and let \(f^*=\inf_{x\in D}f(x)\) be finite. Feasibility of \(\bar x\in D\) gives \(f^*\leq f(\bar x)\), while validity of the independent bound gives \(L\leq f^*\). Hence \[0\leq f(\bar x)-f^*\leq f(\bar x)-L.\] Therefore \((\bar x,L)\) certifies absolute \(\varepsilon\)-global optimality whenever \(f(\bar x)-L\leq\varepsilon\). For a declared scale \(s>0\), it certifies scaled relative tolerance \(\varepsilon\) whenever \((f(\bar x)-L)/s\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible heuristic point and a rigorous lower bound give a computable upper bound on the incumbent's true optimality gap, which certifies absolute or explicitly scaled relative tolerances.
knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Incumbents with Certified Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5 Local, Global, epsilon-Global Minima p. 57

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unverified Primal or Lower-Bound Data Cannot Certify a Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness boundary for heuristic-primal/certified-bound hybrids.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inequality \(L\le f^*\le f(\bar x)\) requires both verified feasibility of \(\bar x\) and rigorous validity of \(L\). If either condition is absent, the computed difference \(f(\bar x)-L\) need not upper-bound the true primal suboptimality and cannot certify global optimality or safe pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A numerical candidate or nonrigorous bound does not yield a global-gap certificate; primal feasibility and lower-bound validity must both be verified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\notin D\ \text{or}\ L\nleq f^*\implies f(\bar x)-L\text{ is not a certified gap in general}.
knowledge_statements.title: Unverified Primal or Lower-Bound Data Cannot Certify a Gap

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotone Strengthening of the Certified Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic bound-management invariant already owned by general bound-gap and global-search leaves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given verified feasible points \(x_1,\ldots,x_p\) and rigorous lower bounds \(L_1,\ldots,L_q\le f^*\), define \(U=\min_i f(x_i)\) and \(L=\max_jL_j\). Then \(L\le f^*\le U\), and adding valid primal or lower-bound information cannot increase \(U-L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combining the best verified incumbent and strongest rigorous lower bound monotonically tightens the certified gap.
assumptions_latex: Each \(L_j\) is a rigorous lower bound on \(f^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\le f^*\le U,\quad U-L\text{ cannot increase as valid information is added}.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Strengthening of the Certified Gap

intermediate_metadata.reason: The locally owned inventory is the heuristic-feasible-primal/rigorous-lower-bound sandwich, absolute and scaled-relative stopping tests, and failure when either side is unverified. Generic monotone bound aggregation was deferred as duplication. Particular lower-bound generators and incumbent-polishing procedures were excluded and cross-indexed.

children.title: Exact Complexity Landscape
children.top_down_role: Classifies exact global optimization by tractable subclasses and broad hardness regimes.

children.title: Polynomially Solvable Nonconvex Islands
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for structurally restricted nonconvex classes admitting efficient exact methods.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local-to-Global Geometry Does Not Imply Polynomial Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between solution geometry and bit complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even if every local minimizer in a class is global, polynomial-time solvability does not follow without a polynomial-time method for finding such a point and a polynomially specified output or approximation criterion. Thus invexity, pseudoconvexity, or another local-to-global property is not by itself a bit-complexity theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local-equals-global geometry establishes validity of solutions, not a polynomial-time method for finding or encoding them.
assumptions_latex: Complexity is measured for encoded instance families in a specified computational model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{all local minima global}\not\Rightarrow\text{polynomial-time global optimization}.
knowledge_statements.title: Local-to-Global Geometry Does Not Imply Polynomial Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic mechanism yielding a polynomially solvable nonconvex class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every rationally encoded \(I\in\mathcal C\) can be transformed in polynomial time and polynomial output size into a convex instance \(T(I)\), with preservation of the global value and polynomial-time recovery of an optimizer or approximation of the declared accuracy. If the target convex class is polynomially solvable in that same output model, then \(\mathcal C\) is polynomially solvable despite the nonconvex original formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact polynomial-size reduction to a tractable convex class transfers polynomial solvability to the original nonconvex class.
assumptions_latex: Forward transformation and recovery have polynomial complexity.
The transformation preserves feasibility and optimal value in the declared output model.
The target convex class is polynomially solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I\mapsto T(I)\text{ exact and polynomial}\Rightarrow\mathcal C\text{ is polynomially solvable}.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Convexification Transfer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete nonquadratic tractable island; quadratic subclasses remain in the quadratic-landscape sibling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\in\mathbb Q[x]\) be given densely and let \(a,b\in\mathbb Q\), \(a\le b\). The problem \(\min_{x\in[a,b]}p(x)\) is exactly solvable in polynomial bit complexity in the dense encoding length of \((p,a,b)\) when an optimizer may be returned as a rational endpoint or as a real algebraic number represented by a square-free defining polynomial and isolating interval. An algorithm isolates the real roots of \(p'\) in \([a,b]\) and compares the objective at those roots and the endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rational univariate polynomial, even when nonconvex and of arbitrary degree, can be minimized exactly on a rational interval in polynomial bit complexity using algebraic-number output.
assumptions_latex: Real algebraic optimizers use defining-polynomial and isolating-interval encodings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{x\in[a,b]}p(x)\text{ and an algebraically encoded minimizer are computable in polynomial bit complexity.}
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial-Time Exact Univariate Polynomial Minimization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact, Decision, and Approximate Polynomial Solvability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates computational claims requiring different output encodings and accuracy guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rationally encoded minimization class \(\mathcal C\), polynomial-time exact optimization returns an attained optimizer and value in a specified finite representation in time polynomial in the input length. Polynomial-time threshold decision decides whether \(v^*(I)\le q\) for a rational threshold \(q\). Polynomial-time additive approximation, with positive rational \(\varepsilon\) encoded in binary, returns a feasible \(x_\varepsilon\) satisfying \(f_I(x_\varepsilon)\le v^*(I)+\varepsilon\) in time polynomial in the input length and the bit length of \(\varepsilon\). These are distinct predicates unless reductions between their output models are established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact optimization, threshold decision, and additive approximation are different polynomial-solvability claims and require explicit output and accuracy models.
assumptions_latex: Instances, thresholds, and tolerances are finitely encoded.
Approximation is asserted only for finite optimal value and requires a feasible returned point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{PolyExact}(\mathcal C),\ \operatorname{PolyDecision}(\mathcal C),\ \operatorname{PolyApprox}(\mathcal C)\text{ are not interchangeable without explicit reductions.}
knowledge_statements.title: Exact, Decision, and Approximate Polynomial Solvability

assumptions_latex: Instances are encoded by rational data and input length is measured in bits.
A structural restriction defines a subclass of otherwise nonconvex optimization problems.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The subclass is a polynomially solvable nonconvex island exactly when global optimization over it has polynomial worst-case bit complexity.

notation.meaning: Binary encoding length of the instance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-complexity definition; no particular tractable subclass is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structurally restricted class \(\mathcal C\) is a polynomially solvable nonconvex island if its members may have nonconvex objectives or feasible regions, yet there exist an exact global-optimization algorithm and a polynomial \(p\) such that every rationally encoded instance \(I\in\mathcal C\) is solved using at most \(p(|I|)\) bit operations. For approximation formulations, the corresponding requirement is a runtime polynomial in \(|I|\) and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\) that returns a feasible point with a stated \(\varepsilon\)-global guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconvex island is polynomially solvable when its structural restrictions permit exact global optimization in time polynomial in the rational input length.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomially Solvable Nonconvex Islands

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is a reasonable role for this taxonomy container, but no source is supplied. Exact continuous global optimization in the bit model requires an explicit output or decision formulation, and the asserted dependence polynomial in log(1/epsilon) is not a generic approximation requirement for nonconvex classes.

children.title: Quadratic Complexity Landscape
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for tractable and hard quadratic subclasses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hard side of the quadratic landscape through weighted MAX-CUT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a graph with nonnegative rational edge weights and weighted Laplacian \(L\succeq0\), \[\max_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}x^{\mathsf T}Lx=\max_{x\in[0,1]^n}x^{\mathsf T}Lx.\] The common value is the maximum cut weight. Therefore deciding whether \[\min_{x\in[0,1]^n}-x^{\mathsf T}Lx\le-\tau\] is NP-hard. Hardness thus holds even for concave quadratic minimization over a unit box.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted MAX-CUT reduces exactly to concave quadratic minimization over a box.
assumptions_latex: Edge weights and threshold \(\tau\) are nonnegative rational data.
\(L\) is the corresponding weighted graph Laplacian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{x\in[0,1]^n}-x^{\mathsf T}Lx\text{ is NP-hard in threshold-decision form}.
knowledge_statements.title: Concave Box-Quadratic NP-Hardness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial side of the rational quadratic complexity boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For rational \(Q\succeq0,c,A,b\), assume \(P=\{x:Ax\le b\}\) is nonempty, bounded, and supplied with polynomially encoded inner and outer radius bounds. Then an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal solution of \[\min_{x\in P}\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\] can be computed in time polynomial in the input length and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rational convex quadratic minimization over a well-described bounded rational polyhedron admits polynomial-time weak optimization.
assumptions_latex: The polyhedron is nonempty and bounded with polynomially encoded geometric bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Runtime is polynomial in the input length and }\log(1/\varepsilon).
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Quadratic Weak Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-Region Exactness Does Not Extend to General QCQP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the single-ball hidden-convexity regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The scalar-shift characterization above relies on one quadratic norm constraint. Replacing the ball by an arbitrary intersection of quadratic inequalities does not preserve that characterization; quadratic syntax alone implies neither zero duality gap nor polynomial solvability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tractability of the one-ball trust-region problem does not extend automatically to general QCQP.
assumptions_latex: The comparison class permits multiple arbitrary quadratic constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{trust-region exactness}\not\Rightarrow\text{general QCQP exactness or tractability}.
knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Exactness Does Not Extend to General QCQP

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-Region Hidden Convexity and Exact Dual Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical tractable indefinite quadratic subclass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For symmetric \(Q\) and \(\Delta>0\), let \[p^*=\min_{\|x\|_2\le\Delta}x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2c^{\mathsf T}x.\] Then \[p^*=\max_{\substack{\lambda\ge0,\ Q+\lambda I\succeq0\\c\in\operatorname{Range}(Q+\lambda I)}}\{-c^{\mathsf T}(Q+\lambda I)^{\dagger}c-\lambda\Delta^2\}.\] Thus the possibly indefinite single-ball problem has zero Lagrangian duality gap, including the stated singular-case range condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The indefinite trust-region quadratic has an exact scalar-shift dual representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^*=\max_{\lambda\ge0}\{-c^{\mathsf T}(Q+\lambda I)^{\dagger}c-\lambda\Delta^2\}\text{ under PSD and range conditions}.
knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Hidden Convexity and Exact Dual Bound

assumptions_latex: Quadratic programs have rational data and are measured in the Turing bit model.
The feasible region is either a rational convex set with convex quadratic objective or a box with an indefinite quadratic objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive-semidefinite quadratic minimization is polynomially solvable under standard convex representations, whereas general indefinite box-constrained quadratic minimization is NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Turing-model boundary between convex and general indefinite quadratic minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(q(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+c^{\mathsf T}x\) with rational symmetric \(Q\). If \(Q\succeq0\) and the rational convex feasible set admits polynomial-time separation, an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal solution can be computed in time polynomial in the input length and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\). Without positive semidefiniteness, global minimization is NP-hard even for bounded box constraints. Thus the sign structure of \(Q\), together with the feasible-set representation, separates a standard polynomially solvable quadratic subclass from the general hard landscape.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex quadratic minimization is polynomially approximable under standard oracle assumptions, while allowing an indefinite quadratic over a box makes global minimization NP-hard.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Complexity Landscape

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A complexity-bound record is appropriate for this leaf, but both sides of the claimed boundary need authoritative citations. Polynomial-time weak optimization from separation requires additional representation, boundedness, and oracle-access conditions, while NP-hardness of indefinite box-constrained quadratic minimization needs a specific theorem or reduction locator.

children.title: General Nonconvex Hardness
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for worst-case hardness of broad continuous global classes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonconvexity Alone Does Not Establish Hardness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on complexity conclusions from geometry alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Nonconvexity of an objective or feasible set does not itself imply NP-hardness. For example, \(\min_{x\in[-2,2]}(x^2-1)^2\) is nonconvex but has the explicit global optimum \(0\) at \(x=\pm1\). Hardness concerns encoded instance families and requires a reduction or hard-subclass containment argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonconvexity is a geometric property, not a hardness proof.
assumptions_latex: Complexity is measured over encoded families of instances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{nonconvexity alone}\not\Rightarrow\text{NP-hardness}.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvexity Alone Does Not Establish Hardness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction principle for exact-value or threshold-decision global optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be NP-hard. Suppose a polynomial-time, polynomial-output-size map \(R\) sends each instance \(I\in\mathcal H\) to an instance \(R(I)\in\mathcal G\) and a rational threshold such that deciding whether the global optimum of \(R(I)\) meets that threshold decides \(I\). Then the threshold-decision version of global optimization over \(\mathcal G\) is NP-hard; consequently an exact polynomial-time optimizer or value algorithm for every instance of \(\mathcal G\) would imply \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A broad global-optimization class inherits NP-hardness from any polynomially embedded hard subclass.
assumptions_latex: The reduction and its output encoding have polynomial size.
The stated optimal-value threshold decides the source instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal H\le_p\mathcal G\Rightarrow\mathcal G\text{ is NP-hard}.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial Hard-Subclass Inheritance

assumptions_latex: Optimization instances are rationally encoded and complexity is measured in the Turing model.
The problem class contains box-constrained indefinite quadratic minimization as a polynomially representable subclass.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact global optimization over the broad class is NP-hard, so a polynomial-time exact algorithm would imply \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subclass-containment hardness statement in the rational Turing model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G\) be a continuous nonconvex minimization class containing every rational box-constrained indefinite quadratic program, with a polynomial-size embedding of each such quadratic instance. Because globally minimizing that subclass is NP-hard, computing \(f^*\) exactly for arbitrary \(I\in\mathcal G\) is NP-hard under polynomial-time reductions. Consequently, unless \(\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}\), no algorithm solves every instance in \(\mathcal G\) exactly in time polynomial in \(|I|\). This worst-case statement does not preclude efficient algorithms for restricted subclasses or useful instance-dependent behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any broad nonconvex class that polynomially contains indefinite box-constrained quadratic optimization inherits its NP-hardness, although restricted subclasses may remain tractable.
knowledge_statements.title: General Nonconvex Hardness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The subclass-containment implication is correctly scoped and a complexity bound fits the container, but its premise relies on an uncited NP-hardness result for box-constrained indefinite quadratic minimization. A specific authoritative theorem or reduction locator is required before the broad-class conclusion can be retained.

children.title: Approximation Complexity
children.top_down_role: Approximation-scheme regimes and inapproximability boundaries.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Global Optimization: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications
