children.title: Variable-Bound Maintenance
children.top_down_role: Storage and propagation of current variable bounds within a modeling system.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical merge operation for independently valid bounds on one current region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every feasible point in the current region satisfies both \(\ell_i^{(1)}\leq x_i\leq u_i^{(1)}\) and \(\ell_i^{(2)}\leq x_i\leq u_i^{(2)}\). Then \(\ell_i'=\max\{\ell_i^{(1)},\ell_i^{(2)}\}\) and \(u_i'=\min\{u_i^{(1)},u_i^{(2)}\}\) define another valid bound interval. If \(\ell_i'>u_i'\), the current region is infeasible. Repeated interval merging is associative, commutative, and idempotent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independently valid bounds are merged by interval intersection; an empty intersection certifies regional infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Both input intervals contain every feasible value of \(x_i\) in the same current region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_i\in[\ell_i',u_i']=[\ell_i^{(1)},u_i^{(1)}]\cap[\ell_i^{(2)},u_i^{(2)}]\quad\text{for every feasible point}.

notation.meaning: Merged authoritative interval for variable i.

knowledge_statements.title: Intersection of Valid Variable Bounds
Variable-Bound Maintenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition for bounds shared by branching, propagation, and reformulation components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each variable \(x_i\), maintain authoritative bounds \([\ell_i^k,u_i^k]\) at region state \(k\). A bound update is admissible when \(\ell_i^k\leq \ell_i^{k+1}\leq u_i^{k+1}\leq u_i^k\) and no feasible point of the current region is removed. Before another relaxation is solved, every bound-dependent constraint, auxiliary-variable range, and solver copy must reference the same version \(k+1\). Empty intervals certify infeasibility only when the tightening operation is valid for the original constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounds may tighten monotonically, but all solver and reformulation copies must use the same version; a validly derived empty interval certifies regional infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Initial bounds satisfy \(\ell_i^0\leq u_i^0\) for every \(i\).
Each tightening rule is valid for all feasible points in the current region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All active model objects use \([\ell_i^{k+1},u_i^{k+1}]\), and \(\ell_i^{k+1}>u_i^{k+1}\) validly certifies infeasibility.

notation.meaning: Authoritative bounds for variable i at version k.

children.title: Lifted-Model Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency between original expressions and lifted auxiliary representations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective agreement between an original model and its exact or relaxed lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)\) be the original objective, let \(y=\phi(x)\), and let \(q(x,y)\) be the lifted objective. Exact objective consistency requires \(q(x,\phi(x))=f(x)\) for every original feasible \(x\). For a minimization relaxation containing every feasible graph point, the weaker condition \(q(x,\phi(x))\leq f(x)\) is sufficient for lower-bound validity. A projected incumbent must nevertheless be evaluated using \(f\), unless objective equality has been validated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact lift preserves objective values on the defining graph. A minimization relaxation may underestimate them, but projected incumbents require the original objective unless equality is verified.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi(x)\) is defined at every original feasible point.
The lifted relaxation contains \((x,\phi(x))\) for every original feasible \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(x,\phi(x))=f(x)\text{ for exact objective consistency};\qquad q(x,\phi(x))\leq f(x)\text{ suffices for minimization lower-bound validity}.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Objective Consistency
Lifted-Model Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection and graph-consistency requirements for auxiliary variables in lifted models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original feasible set be \(F=\{x:g(x)\leq0,\ h(x)=0\}\) on a box \(B\), and introduce auxiliaries \(y=\phi(x)\). A lifted formulation with feasible set \(L_B\) is exact when \(\operatorname{proj}_x L_B=F\cap B\) and every lifted feasible point satisfies \(y=\phi(x)\). A lifted relaxation \(R_B\) is consistent when \(\{(x,\phi(x)):x\in F\cap B\}\subseteq R_B\); any point returned as an original feasible incumbent must additionally satisfy the exact defining equalities for its auxiliaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact lift projects to the original feasible set and satisfies all defining equations; a relaxed lift must contain every lifted original feasible point.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi\) is defined on the current box \(B\).
Projection retains precisely the original variables \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactness gives \(\operatorname{proj}_x L_B=F\cap B\); relaxation consistency gives \(\operatorname{graph}(\phi|_{F\cap B})\subseteq R_B\).

notation.meaning: Exact lifted feasible set on B.

children.title: Bound-Synchronization Failures
children.top_down_role: Implementation failures caused by stale or inconsistent bound information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp containment condition for reusing bound-dependent relaxations after bound changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q(\widehat B)\) be an outer relaxation certified for every graph point whose original variables lie in \(\widehat B\). Reusing it on a current region \(B\) is valid whenever \(B\subseteq\widehat B\), although regeneration on \(B\) may strengthen it. If \(B\nsubseteq\widehat B\), the certificate for \(Q(\widehat B)\) gives no validity guarantee on \(B\setminus\widehat B\); reuse may exclude feasible graph points and produce an invalid lower bound. Enlargement therefore requires regeneration or an independent extension certificate, whereas tightening within the generating box preserves validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation generated on one box remains valid on contained tighter regions, but reuse outside that box is unsafe without revalidation.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(\widehat B)\) is certified as an outer relaxation only on \(\widehat B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\subseteq\widehat B\) implies outer validity is preserved on \(B\); if \(B\nsubseteq\widehat B\), validity does not follow from the original certificate.

notation.meaning: Relaxation generated and certified on box \(\widehat B\).

knowledge_statements.title: Validity-Domain Containment Boundary
Bound-Synchronization Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of relaxation validity when bound-dependent envelopes use incompatible regional bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w=xy\), McCormick inequalities generated from a box \(B=[\ell_x,u_x]\times[\ell_y,u_y]\) are valid on \(B\). If a worker processes a region \(B'\) but installs inequalities generated from an incompatible box \(\widehat B\) with \(B'\nsubseteq\widehat B\), validity can fail. For example, \(B'=[0,1]^2\) and \(\widehat B=[0,\tfrac12]^2\) produce \(w\leq\tfrac12x\); the graph point \((x,y,w)=(1,1,1)\) belongs to \(B'\) but violates this inequality. Thus the resulting lower bound need not be valid for \(B'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An envelope built for bounds that do not contain the processed region can cut off true graph points, making the resulting regional lower bound invalid.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation contains bound-dependent McCormick inequalities for \(w=xy\).
The processed region is not contained in the box used to generate those inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation may exclude feasible graph points, so its optimum is not necessarily a valid lower bound on the processed region.

notation.meaning: Region currently processed by a worker.
Box used to generate stale or incompatible envelopes.

children.title: Primal Incumbent Generation

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Incumbent Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible-point certificate for objective upper bounds in minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in F\}\). A candidate \(\bar x\) becomes a primal incumbent only after validation establishes \(\bar x\in F\), including variable bounds, inequalities, and equalities under the prescribed feasibility tolerances. Its value \(U=f(\bar x)\) then satisfies \(p^*\leq U\). Among validated candidates \(x^1,\ldots,x^m\), retain \(U_m=\min_j f(x^j)\) and an attaining point. An unvalidated or infeasible candidate supplies no certified upper bound, regardless of its objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any validated feasible point gives an upper bound for a minimization problem; the best validated candidate is retained as the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The global problem is a minimization problem with feasible set \(F\).
Objective values are evaluated consistently with the original model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in F\) implies \(p^*\leq f(\bar x)\), and \(U_m=\min_{1\leq j\leq m}f(x^j)\) is the incumbent bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity principle for linear, convex, or conic regional lower-bounding solves.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem on region \(B\), let \(F_B\) be its feasible set and let \(R_B\) be a solver-compatible linear, convex, or conic relaxation in the same variable space satisfying \(F_B\subseteq R_B\). If the relaxation objective \(\underline f\) obeys \(\underline f(x)\leq f(x)\) for every \(x\in F_B\), then any certified relaxation optimum \(L_B=\inf_{x\in R_B}\underline f(x)\) satisfies \(L_B\leq\inf_{x\in F_B}f(x)\). An infeasible relaxation certifies regional infeasibility, while an unbounded or numerically uncertified solve does not provide a finite certified lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver returns a valid regional lower bound when its relaxation contains the original regional feasible set and its relaxation objective underestimates the original objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Subproblem Solvers

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Basic Concepts of Global Optimization p. 33

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certification of a relaxation lower bound independently of a potentially inexact primal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization relaxation with primal optimal value \(v_R\) and a dual satisfying weak duality. For every validated dual-feasible point \(\bar y\) with finite dual objective \(d(\bar y)\), \(d(\bar y)\leq v_R\). If the relaxation is a valid lower-bounding model for the original regional problem with value \(p_B^*\), then \(d(\bar y)\leq v_R\leq p_B^*\). Thus \(d(\bar y)\) is a certified regional lower bound even when a returned primal point is approximate. A relaxation-primal feasible objective generally bounds \(v_R\) from above and is not, by itself, a lower-bound certificate for \(p_B^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A validated dual-feasible objective certifies a regional lower bound by weak duality; an approximate primal objective generally does not.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation is valid for the original regional minimization problem.
The relaxation dual satisfies weak duality.
\(\bar y\) is validated as dual feasible and has a finite dual objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d(\bar y)\leq v_R\leq p_B^*.

notation.meaning: Objective value of a validated dual-feasible point.

children.title: Warm-Start Transfer Interface

children.title: Warm-Start State Transfer
children.top_down_role: Reuse of solver state across related relaxation or local-search subproblems.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-neutral transfer of supported internal initialization state, excluding incumbent-solution transfer and relaxation-basis reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given predecessor state \(s_p\) and successor model \(Q_c\), map only state fields for which the receiving interface supplies a compatible successor object and representation. Discard every unmapped or incompatible field, submit the accepted partial state \(s_c\) only as initialization data, and validate all feasibility, bounds, termination tests, and certificates from computations performed on \(Q_c\). Rejection of any or all transferred fields leaves correctness unchanged and permits an ordinary initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Import only receiver-recognized compatible state, treat it solely as initialization, and certify every result using the successor model.
assumptions_latex: The receiving solver identifies which state fields and successor objects it supports.
Rejected or absent state can be replaced by an ordinary initialization.
The successor solve validates its outputs against \(Q_c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_c\) may affect initialization and performance, but no correctness claim for \(Q_c\) is inherited from \(s_p\).

notation.meaning: Predecessor solver state offered for transfer.

review_flags: Exact accepted state fields remain solver-interface dependent.
knowledge_statements.title: Receiver-Validated Partial-State Import
Warm-Start State Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility-checked transfer of solver state between related regional subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_p\) be a solved parent subproblem with state \(s_p\), and let \(Q_c\) be a child or updated subproblem. Map state components by persistent variable and constraint identifiers, discard components whose dimensions or mathematical meanings changed, project primal values onto the bounds of \(Q_c\), and retain dual or basis information only when its solver-specific compatibility conditions hold. Initialize the solver for \(Q_c\) with the accepted partial state \(s_c\). Regardless of transfer, certify all bounds and feasibility using \(Q_c\), never the predecessor state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer only identifier-compatible solver data, repair or discard invalid components, and certify every result against the new subproblem.
assumptions_latex: The predecessor and successor models expose stable identifiers for transferable objects.
The receiving solver permits partial warm starts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transferred state initializes \(Q_c\), but correctness and certification depend solely on solving and validating \(Q_c\).

children.title: Incumbent Solution Transfer
children.top_down_role: Reuse of feasible solutions across nodes, formulations, or solver components.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion for transferring an incumbent from a parent region to a nested successor region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_C=F_P\cap C\) be the feasible set of a child region. If \(\bar x\in F_P\) is a validated parent incumbent, then it is a feasible child incumbent if and only if \(\bar x\in C\). When parent and child retain the same original objective \(f\), the inherited objective value is \(U_C=f(\bar x)\). If \(\bar x\notin C\), the point remains feasible for the original problem but is not a child-incumbent certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A validated parent incumbent transfers to a nested child exactly when it satisfies the child's added regional restrictions.
assumptions_latex: Parent and child use the same original objective function.
\(F_P\) is the original feasible set restricted to the parent region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar x\in F_C\iff(\bar x\in F_P\ \wedge\ \bar x\in C).
knowledge_statements.title: Nested-Region Incumbent Inheritance
Incumbent Solution Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Revalidation rule for incumbents transferred across regional or reformulated models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a source model supplies an incumbent \(z_s\), and let \(M\) map its original-variable components to a target candidate \(x_t=M(z_s)\). The transfer certifies an incumbent for the target minimization problem only if target-side validation proves \(x_t\in F_t\). Then \(U_t=f_t(x_t)\) is a valid target upper bound. Auxiliary values may be reconstructed from target defining equations, but source feasibility, source tolerances, or equality of variable names alone cannot replace target validation. If validation fails, retain \(x_t\) only as a heuristic starting point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transferred solution becomes a target incumbent only after target-side feasibility validation; otherwise it is merely a heuristic start.
assumptions_latex: A mapping \(M\) between source and target original variables is defined.
The target problem is a minimization problem with feasible set \(F_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_t\in F_t\) implies \(p_t^*\leq U_t=f_t(x_t)\); failed validation yields no target upper-bound certificate.

children.title: Relaxation-Basis Reuse
children.top_down_role: Transfer of reusable relaxation-solver information between related subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Basis Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility conditions for reusing an LP relaxation basis after model changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a linear relaxation in standard form, a stored basis indexed by \(B\) may be reused directly only when the successor relaxation preserves the corresponding rows, columns, coefficient matrix entries, and basis dimension. With successor right-hand side \(b'\), the reused basic primal vector is \(x_B'=A_B^{-1}b'\); it is primal feasible exactly when \(x_B'\geq0\). If costs change to \(c'\), dual feasibility additionally requires the successor reduced costs to have the signs prescribed by the minimization convention. Otherwise the basis is merely an advanced start and must be repaired by the LP solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An LP basis remains directly usable only under structural compatibility; changed bounds or costs may destroy primal or dual feasibility and require basis repair.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation is represented in a fixed standard-form convention.
The stored basis matrix \(A_B\) remains nonsingular in the successor model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Direct primal reuse is feasible iff \(A_B^{-1}b'\geq0\); optimal reuse also requires successor dual feasibility.

notation.meaning: Basis matrix selected by basis index set B.

children.title: Transfer Degradation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cases where inherited information becomes stale, incompatible, or counterproductive.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compatibility and Performance Limits of Warm-Start Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates transfer admissibility from any claim of computational benefit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s\) be predecessor solver state and let \(C_T(s)\) be the subset whose identifiers, dimensions, meanings, and numerical domains are compatible with a successor model \(T\). Only \(C_T(s)\) may be offered as successor initialization, and no inherited component certifies successor feasibility, optimality, or an objective bound without successor validation. If \(C_T(s)=\varnothing\), the transfer interface supplies no warm-start state. Even when \(C_T(s)\neq\varnothing\), compatibility alone implies no solver-independent reduction in iterations or runtime relative to an initialization that ignores the state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only compatible state may be transferred, transferred state carries no certificate by itself, and compatibility does not guarantee a speedup.
assumptions_latex: Every transferred component has a defined successor interpretation.
Successor certificates are validated against the successor model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_T(s)=\varnothing\Rightarrow\text{no state is transferred};\qquad C_T(s)\neq\varnothing\not\Rightarrow\text{a solver-independent performance improvement}.

notation.meaning: Subset of predecessor state compatible with successor model T.

review_flags: Specific claims about runtime degradation from scaling, active-set, or structural changes require solver-specific evidence.
knowledge_statements.title: Compatibility and Performance Limits of Warm-Start Transfer
Transfer Degradation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regimes in which warm starts lose compatibility or computational value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Warm-start transfer provides no correctness guarantee and may lose computational value when the successor differs substantially from its predecessor. Degradation occurs if branching fixes many previously free variables, reformulation adds or removes rows or columns, scaling changes materially, the active set changes, or inherited primal and dual values violate new bounds or constraints. In the limiting structural regime where no stored component has a compatible successor identifier, the admissible transferred state is empty and the method reduces to a cold start. Any incompatible component must be discarded rather than used to certify feasibility, optimality, or a bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Large structural, scaling, or active-set changes can erase warm-start value; with no compatible state components, transfer reduces to a cold start.
assumptions_latex: Warm-start components are accepted only after successor-model compatibility checks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the compatible component set is empty, then \(s_c=\varnothing\) and initialization is equivalent to a cold start.

notation.meaning: State admissible for the successor solve.

review_flags: performance-degradation regimes require empirical or solver-specific sources

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits Transfer Degradation Regimes. Claims that particular structural, scaling, and active-set changes reduce computational value are empirical or solver-specific, and the asserted equivalence to a cold start depends on initialization semantics. No supporting source is supplied.

children.title: Concurrent Global Execution Regimes
children.top_down_role: Concurrency structures for independent or weakly coupled global subproblems.

children.title: Parallel Region Processing
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for concurrent spatial subproblem evaluation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient scheduling condition for inheriting a regional method's serial convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the committed operations of a parallel region-processing run can be ordered as a valid execution of an underlying serial region method: each region has unique ownership while processed; each committed split replaces its parent by covering children; pruning uses valid certificates; failed or abandoned work is safely requeued; and every persistently eligible region is eventually committed. Then any convergence conclusion proved for every fair serial execution of that method also holds for the parallel run. Assignment and completion orders may differ provided the committed history satisfies these conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parallel run inherits a fair serial method's convergence guarantee when its committed history is serializable, coverage preserving, certificate safe, and free of lost or starved regions.
assumptions_latex: The underlying regional method converges for every fair serial execution satisfying its stated hypotheses.
Committed ownership and replacement operations are serializable.
Every persistently eligible region is eventually committed.
No assigned region is silently lost, and all pruning certificates are valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parallel run inherits the convergence conclusion of the corresponding fair serial execution.
review_flags: The conclusion is conditional on the exact hypotheses and conclusion of the underlying serial convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.title: Serializable Fair Parallel Processing
Parallel Region Processing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global-bound invariant for concurrent processing of a spatial partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let active regions \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\) cover every not-yet-pruned feasible point of a minimization problem. Worker \(i\) computes a certified lower bound \(L_i\) for \(B_i\) and may return validated feasible points. The global lower bound is \(L=\min_{i\in A}L_i\), where \(A\) indexes active regions, while the global incumbent is the least objective value among all validated feasible points. A region may be pruned when it is infeasible or when \(L_i\geq U\), subject to the chosen optimality tolerance. Processing order and concurrency do not alter these validity conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel workers bound separate active regions; the minimum active lower bound and best validated incumbent remain the global certificates.
assumptions_latex: Active regions cover all feasible points not already validly pruned.
Every reported regional lower bound and incumbent is certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=\min_{i\in A}L_i\leq p^*\leq U\), and regions satisfying \(L_i\geq U\) may be pruned.

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound for region i.

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

review_flags: parallel execution extension is not explicit in the supplied locator

source_witnesses.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

The cited partition-strategy locator does not explicitly support concurrent processing, aggregation, or concurrency-independent validity, so a parallel global-optimization source is required.

children.title: Distributed Bound-Incumbent Coordination
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for coordinating global bounds across workers.

children.title: Distributed Bound Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Collection and reconciliation of bound information from multiple workers.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of distributed lower-bound aggregation when an unresolved region is omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two unresolved regions \(R_1,R_2\) have valid lower bounds \(L_1=0\) and \(L_2=10\), with \(p^*=0\) attained in \(R_1\). If the aggregation ledger omits \(R_1\), then \(\widehat L=10>p^*\). Thus the minimum over an incomplete ledger need not be a global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting an unresolved region can make the aggregated lower bound exceed the true optimum and invalidate a gap certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(R_1\cup R_2\) contains every unresolved feasible point.
The ledger contains \(R_2\) but omits unresolved region \(R_1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat L=10>p^*=0\), so the incomplete-ledger aggregate is invalid.

notation.meaning: Aggregate computed from the incomplete ledger.

knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete-Ledger Aggregation Failure
Distributed Bound Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation invariant for distributed regional bounds and feasible incumbents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At aggregation epoch \(t\), let \(A_t\) contain every active region not validly pruned, and let \(L_i^t\) be a certified lower bound for region \(i\). Define \(L^t=\min_{i\in A_t}L_i^t\). Let \(U^t\) be the minimum objective value among all globally validated incumbents received by the epoch. If the active-region ledger is complete and each bound refers to the current region version, then \(L^t\leq p^*\leq U^t\). For absolute tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), the inequality \(U^t-L^t\leq\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate the minimum current active-region lower bound and best validated incumbent; with a complete fresh ledger, their gap certifies global accuracy.
assumptions_latex: The active-region ledger is complete at epoch \(t\).
Each \(L_i^t\) is valid for the recorded current version of region \(i\).
Every value contributing to \(U^t\) comes from a globally validated feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L^t\leq p^*\leq U^t\), and \(U^t-L^t\leq\varepsilon\) certifies absolute \(\varepsilon\)-global optimality.

notation.meaning: Complete active-region index set at aggregation epoch t.

source_refs.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

review_flags: distributed freshness and ledger conditions need a direct parallel-optimization source

source_witnesses.locator: Part Two. Partition Strategies in Global Optimization: The Continuous and the Lipschitzian Case p. 39

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits Distributed Bound Aggregation, and the gap certificate follows under the stated complete-ledger and current-version assumptions. The supplied serial partition-strategy locator does not support distributed epochs, freshness, or ledger consistency; a direct distributed global-optimization source is required.

children.title: Incumbent Dissemination
children.top_down_role: Distribution of improved feasible solutions across active workers.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic reconciliation of replicated feasible-incumbent records.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a certified incumbent record be \(r=(v,x,q)\), where \(x\in F\), \(v=f(x)\), and \(q\) is a deterministic tie key. Order records lexicographically by \((v,q)\) and set \(r\sqcap s=\min\{r,s\}\). Then \(\sqcap\) is associative, commutative, and idempotent. For any finite set of generated records, or after a quiescent time following which no better record is generated, eventual delivery and repeated merging make every participating replica equal to the least disseminated record, independently of message order and duplication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deterministic minimum merging is order-independent and duplicate-tolerant; after generation quiesces and delivery completes, replicas agree on the best disseminated incumbent.
assumptions_latex: Every record contains a validated feasible point and its correctly evaluated objective.
The tie key induces a total order.
Every relevant generated record is eventually delivered to each participating replica.
The generated record set is finite, or generation eventually quiesces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sqcap\) is associative, commutative, and idempotent, and replicas eventually agree on \(\bigsqcap r\).
knowledge_statements.title: Order-Independent Incumbent Merge
Incumbent Dissemination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asynchronous broadcast of improving feasible objectives in distributed minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For workers \(i=1,\ldots,p\), initialize the shared incumbent value \(U=+\infty\). Whenever worker \(i\) obtains a feasible point \(x_i\in F\) with \(f(x_i)<U_i\), it atomically records or broadcasts \((f(x_i),x_i)\). Upon receiving \((v,x)\), worker \(j\) replaces its local pair \((U_j,\hat x_j)\) by \((v,x)\) exactly when \(v<U_j\). Ties are resolved by a fixed deterministic rule. On termination, output a feasible stored point \(\hat x\) attaining the smallest disseminated value \(U=\min_i U_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers broadcast improving feasible solutions, retain the best received objective, and return the best disseminated incumbent under deterministic tie-breaking.
assumptions_latex: Every accepted message contains \(x\in F\) and its correctly evaluated value \(f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\) is nonincreasing and equals the smallest objective value among all successfully disseminated feasible points.

notation.meaning: worker i's local incumbent upper bound

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: monotone asynchronous incumbent broadcast is a standard distributed branch-and-bound coordination rule
distributed-global-optimization source with an exact protocol is required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but no inspectable source supports this exact asynchronous protocol. The statement also mixes an atomic shared record with broadcast semantics, does not initialize each local U_i, and needs a termination or message-delivery condition for the final minimum claim.

children.title: Stale-Information Control
children.top_down_role: Management of delayed bound or incumbent updates in distributed search.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Control of delayed regional-bound messages after region or relaxation changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Associate each represented region \(R\) with a monotonically increasing version \(
u(R)\). A message \((R,
u,L)\) may replace the stored lower bound only when \(
u=
u(R)\) and \(L\) is certified for that version's region and relaxation. Older messages are discarded. After a split, contraction, or reformulation changes the version, an earlier bound may support pruning or aggregation only if an independent certificate proves it valid on the current represented region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Install only version-matching certified regional bounds; discard or independently revalidate bounds after their region or relaxation changes.
assumptions_latex: Each bound certificate identifies its region and relaxation validity domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every installed bound is valid for the current represented region, and obsolete messages cannot alone justify pruning or aggregation.

notation.meaning: Current version of represented region R.

knowledge_statements.title: Version-Validated Bound Installation
Stale-Information Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-delay condition for local bounds and incumbents used by distributed workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^k\) denote the globally committed coordination state after event \(k\), and let worker \(i\) act at event \(k\) using \(z^{\tau_i(k)}\). Bounded staleness with delay \(D\in\mathbb N\) means \[0\le k-\tau_i(k)\le D\] for every active worker and event. An incumbent-dependent pruning decision is admissible only if its incumbent value is no smaller than the latest committed feasible value known to the decision mechanism; a bound update computed from stale data must remain mathematically valid for the represented region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each worker uses information at most D events old, and stale data may affect pruning only when feasibility and bound validity remain preserved.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No accepted coordination decision depends on information older than \(D\) events, and accepted pruning retains its stated validity.

notation.meaning: committed coordination state at event k
state index read by worker i at event k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bounded-delay reads are a standard asynchronous-computation consistency condition
exact source connecting bounded staleness to globally valid pruning is required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded-delay condition fits the leaf and is mathematically plausible, but the specialized connection between stale incumbents, bound updates, and globally valid pruning requires an exact distributed global-optimization source.

children.title: Asynchronous Consistency Regimes
children.top_down_role: Consistency requirements under asynchronous global-search execution.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample separating eventual from uniformly bounded visibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For committed update \(j\), let each worker observe that update only after \(j\) later communication events. Every update is eventually observed, but the delays \(1,2,3,\ldots\) are unbounded, so no finite \(D\) satisfies bounded staleness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All updates may arrive eventually even though their visibility delays grow without bound.
assumptions_latex: There are infinitely many committed updates and continuing communication events.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{eventual visibility}\not\Longrightarrow\text{bounded staleness}.

notation.meaning: update index and assigned visibility delay

knowledge_statements.title: Eventual Visibility without Bounded Staleness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested visibility guarantees for versioned distributed coordination state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let committed coordination states have monotonically increasing versions. A read is strongly consistent when it returns the latest committed version at its linearization point. It has bounded staleness \(D\) when its returned version trails the latest relevant committed version by at most \(D\). Visibility is eventual when every committed update, or a later state subsuming it, is observed after finite delay by every perpetually active worker that continues communicating.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong, bounded-staleness, and eventual consistency describe progressively weaker guarantees on when committed coordination state becomes visible.
assumptions_latex: Coordination states are versioned and later versions subsume incorporated updates.
Perpetually active workers continue to perform communication steps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{strong}\Longrightarrow\text{bounded staleness with }D=0\Longrightarrow\text{eventual visibility}.
knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Visibility Regimes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on declaring completion from asynchronously observed search state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A worker-local gap \(U-L_w\le\varepsilon\) does not certify global completion while live, queued, transferred, or completed-but-unmerged regions remain unaccounted for. Termination requires a consistent cut of the distributed execution that accounts for every search region and combines their valid bounds with a verified incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local small gap is not a global certificate unless a consistent distributed snapshot accounts for all work.
assumptions_latex: Search regions may be owned, queued, transferred, or completed at different workers.
The claimed completion is based on global bound closure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{global completion requires complete consistent accounting of distributed work}.

notation.meaning: lower-bound state visible to worker w

knowledge_statements.title: Consistent-Cut Requirement for Global Termination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strictness of the nested asynchronous visibility guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Strong consistency is the zero-staleness case. Bounded staleness implies eventual visibility under continuing communication, but eventual visibility supplies no uniform finite staleness bound. Neither converse holds in general.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The consistency regimes form a strict implication hierarchy rather than an exclusive classification.
assumptions_latex: The versioned-state and communication assumptions of the visibility-regime definition hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{strong}\Rightarrow\text{bounded}\Rightarrow\text{eventual},\qquad \text{converses fail in general}.
knowledge_statements.title: Consistency-Regime Implication Boundary
Asynchronous Consistency Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three consistency regimes for distributed bound-incumbent state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For committed states \(z^0,z^1,\ldots\), classify an asynchronous execution as: strong if every operation reads the latest committed state; bounded-delay if there exists \(D<\infty\) such that every read at event \(k\) returns some \(z^{\tau(k)}\) with \(k-D\le\tau(k)\le k\); or eventual if every committed update is observed by every perpetually active worker after finitely many later events. In every regime, incumbent updates use a minimum reduction and lower-bound updates may be combined only by validity-preserving operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Executions are strongly consistent, bounded-delay, or eventually consistent according to when committed updates become visible, while bound-validity invariants remain mandatory.
assumptions_latex: \(z^k\) is a totally ordered sequence of committed states.
Every perpetually active worker performs infinitely many communication steps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The execution belongs to the stated regime precisely when its read indices satisfy the corresponding visibility condition.

notation.meaning: commit index observed at event k

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: strong, bounded-delay, and eventual consistency are standard asynchronous coordination regimes
a distributed global-optimization source is needed for the bound-validity specialization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but no source supports the stated optimization-specific consistency regimes and validity invariants. Strong, bounded-delay, and eventual consistency are generally overlapping rather than an exclusive classification, so the intended hierarchy also needs authoritative clarification.

children.title: Large-Scale Decomposable Models
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for globally difficult models with exploitable block structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependency-graph representation of block separability and interface structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For variable blocks \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\), define an undirected coupling graph \(H=(\{1,\ldots,m\},E)\) with \(\{i,j\}\in E\) whenever an objective term, constraint, or shared auxiliary relation depends jointly on blocks \(i\) and \(j\). If \(H\) has components \(C_1,\ldots,C_k\) and no omitted global relation couples different components, then the model separates into independent component subproblems. More generally, fixing the variables in a vertex separator removes graph-recorded dependencies between the remaining components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coupling graph records block interactions: disconnected components are independent, and small separators identify interfaces whose fixation separates the remaining model.
assumptions_latex: Every model expression has a well-defined set of dependent variable blocks.
All cross-block objective terms, constraints, and shared auxiliary relations are represented in \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Disconnected components yield independent subproblems; fixing a vertex separator removes the recorded dependencies between remaining components.

notation.meaning: Connected component of the coupling graph.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Coupling Graph
Large-Scale Decomposable Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-structured continuous global models coupled through a comparatively small interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A continuous global optimization model is block decomposable if its variables admit a partition \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\), with \(x_i\in X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\), such that \[\min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)+h(A_1x_1,\ldots,A_mx_m):x_i\in X_i,\ g_i(x_i)\le0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m B_i x_i=b\right\}.\] The block functions or sets may be nonconvex. The model is large-scale decomposable when the aggregate block dimension is large while evaluation, relaxation, or optimization can be performed blockwise except for the displayed coupling terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A large model is decomposable when most objectives and constraints separate by variable blocks, leaving only limited linking terms or constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Removing \(h\) and the linking equality separates the model into \(m\) independent block subproblems.

notation.meaning: block contribution to the linking constraints

children.title: Structured Test-Problem Families
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for tests grouped by analytic model structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for parametric or randomized family generators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(G(\theta,\xi)\) generates members of a family with declared invariant class \(\mathcal S\), every admissible parameter and seed must produce a well-defined member of \(\mathcal S\). Any rejection, conditioning, or repair rule is part of the generator specification because it changes the induced collection or distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family generator must preserve every declared invariant and disclose all rejection or repair rules.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a parametric or randomized instance generator.
\(\mathcal S\) is the declared structural class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G(\theta,\xi)\in\mathcal S\quad\text{for every admissible }(\theta,\xi).
knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Preserving Instance Generation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indexed test instances sharing declared analytic invariants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structured test-problem family is an indexed collection \(\mathcal P=\{P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\) whose members share a declared analytic template, such as a function class, constraint class, separability pattern, sparsity pattern, symmetry, or degree structure. Coordinates of \(\theta\) vary dimensions or numerical data. Reference solutions and certified bounds are solution metadata, not determinants of analytic family membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured test family varies data or size within a shared declared analytic model template.
assumptions_latex: Every member is well-defined on its declared domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_\theta\in\mathcal S\quad\text{for every }\theta\in\Theta,
knowledge_statements.title: Structured Test-Problem Family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between analytic classification and solution metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An incorrect or missing reference optimum may invalidate accuracy scoring but does not alter membership in a family defined by analytic structure. Structural classification changes only if the model or its declared structural metadata changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reference values affect scoring, not analytically defined family membership.
assumptions_latex: Family membership is defined by analytic model structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{correcting reference metadata leaves analytic family membership unchanged}.
knowledge_statements.title: Reference-Value Independence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Systematic variation of size and numerical features within a family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A controlled family records independently varying features—such as dimension, density, coefficient scale, conditioning surrogate, or constraint count—as distinct coordinates of \(\theta\). A performance trend attributed to one coordinate is interpretable only after the remaining varying coordinates are fixed, stratified, randomized under a declared design, or included in the analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Declared scaling coordinates prevent difficulty trends from being silently confounded with other family changes.
assumptions_latex: Instances are compared across multiple parameter values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{every reported scaling trend is indexed by declared family coordinates}.
knowledge_statements.title: Controlled Scaling Coordinates
Structured Test-Problem Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parametric benchmark families grouped by invariant analytic structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structured test-problem family is an indexed collection \(\mathcal P=\{P_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\) of continuous optimization instances for which each \(P_\theta\) specifies an objective \(f_\theta:X_\theta\to\mathbb R\), a feasible set \(F_\theta\subseteq X_\theta\), and metadata describing a common analytic template. The template fixes structural features such as separability, polynomial degree, sparsity pattern, constraint class, or known symmetries, while \(\theta\) controls dimensions and numerical data. Any claimed reference optimum or lower bound is stored separately from the structural classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured benchmark family varies dimensions or data within a shared analytic template and separates structural metadata from claimed solution values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Instances share declared structural invariants while permitting controlled variation through \(\theta\).

notation.meaning: test instance indexed by parameter theta

children.title: Reproducible Evaluation Protocol System
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for comparative computational evidence.

children.title: Benchmark Protocol Design
children.top_down_role: Experimental designs for comparing continuous global optimization methods.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replication condition for stochastic solver benchmarks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When outcomes depend on randomness, independent replicates are runs assigned independent seeds or random streams under the declared randomization design. Multiple measurements extracted from one run are repeated observations, not independent replicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic benchmarks count independently randomized runs, not within-run observations, as independent replicates.
assumptions_latex: At least one evaluated pipeline is stochastic.
Variability or inferential summaries are reported.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: n_{\mathrm{rep}}=\text{number of independently randomized runs}.
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Replication Unit

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predeclared experimental rules for a reproducible solver benchmark.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A benchmark protocol declares before confirmatory comparison the instance population or sample, solver configurations, resource-accounting rule, execution environment, randomness and replication policy, feasibility and termination conventions, outcome fields, missing-run treatment, and statistical summaries. It also defines an unambiguous map from each admissible run record to its reported outcome or failure category.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A benchmark protocol predeclares what is run, under which resources and conventions, and how every run becomes a reported outcome.
assumptions_latex: The protocol identifies its comparison objective or estimand.
Every admissible run can be assigned a declared outcome or failure category.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{run record}\longmapsto\text{declared outcome or failure category}.
knowledge_statements.title: Benchmark Protocol Design

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between predeclared and exploratory benchmark analyses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Selecting instances, budgets, metrics, exclusions, or solver settings after inspecting comparative outcomes changes the analysis being estimated. The adaptation must be disclosed and treated as exploratory unless evaluated on independent confirmation data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outcome-driven protocol changes cannot be presented as an unchanged predeclared comparison.
assumptions_latex: The comparison is claimed to evaluate a prespecified population, metric, or hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{undisclosed outcome adaptation}\Longrightarrow\text{no confirmatory interpretation}.
knowledge_statements.title: Outcome-Adaptive Protocol Boundary

children.title: Reproducibility Artifacts
children.top_down_role: Data, configurations, environments, and records supporting computational reproduction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition for reconstruction without hidden mutable inputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bundle is dependency-closed relative to its declared platform when every non-platform input required to parse instances, build or invoke the solver, execute runs, and parse outcomes is included immutably or referenced by an immutable retrievable identifier. An omitted mutable dependency prevents reconstruction from the bundle alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every non-platform workflow dependency must be included or immutably identified.
assumptions_latex: The target platform and execution workflow are declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{dependency closure is necessary for reconstruction without hidden mutable inputs}.
knowledge_statements.title: Artifact Dependency Closure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Artifact Identity Is Not Outcome Reproduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between byte identity and successful experimental reproduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Matching cryptographic digests against a trusted manifest establishes artifact-byte identity subject to the digest's integrity assumptions. It does not establish correctness, executability, or reproduction of reported outcomes; those claims require validation and rerun evidence under the protocol's deterministic equality or stochastic acceptance rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Checksums identify archived bytes but do not prove correctness or successful reproduction.
assumptions_latex: The manifest is trusted and the digest comparison is performed correctly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{digest equality}\not\Longrightarrow\text{correctness or outcome reproduction}.
knowledge_statements.title: Artifact Identity Is Not Outcome Reproduction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computational objects supporting identification, inspection, and rerunning of a benchmark.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reproducibility artifact bundle preserves or immutably identifies the benchmark instances, solver implementation and version, build and execution instructions, environment specification, configurations and seeds, raw run records, parsing code, and an integrity manifest. The bundle states its target platform and any externally supplied dependencies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reproducibility bundle preserves the data, implementation, environment, configuration, raw records, parsing workflow, and integrity metadata needed to inspect and rerun an experiment.
assumptions_latex: Every external object is identified by a retrievable immutable reference or explicitly declared unavailable.
The target platform boundary is stated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{bundle contents identify the computational workflow and its recorded inputs and outputs}.
knowledge_statements.title: Reproducibility Artifact Bundle
Reproducibility Artifacts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Artifact bundle permitting independent reconstruction and checking of benchmark outcomes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a benchmark execution, a reproducibility artifact is a bundle \(A=(C,D,E,P,R,H)\) containing immutable solver code or binaries \(C\), instances \(D\), environment specification \(E\), parameter and seed files \(P\), raw run records \(R\), and cryptographic digests \(H\). It certifies artifact identity when every digest matches its archived object, and it supports result reconstruction when an independent execution of the prescribed workflow maps \((C,D,E,P)\) to outcomes within the protocol's declared deterministic equality or stochastic acceptance criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reproducibility bundle records implementations, data, environment, parameters, seeds, raw logs, and hashes sufficient to identify and reconstruct an experiment.
assumptions_latex: Every object referenced by \(A\) is retrievable.
The protocol states its deterministic or stochastic acceptance criterion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Matching \(H\) verifies artifact identity; satisfying the acceptance criterion verifies reconstruction of the reported outcomes.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: code, data, environments, parameters, raw logs, and checksums are standard reproducibility artifacts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the proposed artifact bundle or reconstruction criterion. The bundle is more naturally a representation than a mathematical certificate; matching digests certifies object identity only, not the substantive correctness or reproducibility of benchmark outcomes.

children.title: Cross-Solver Comparability
children.top_down_role: Conditions required for meaningful comparison across solver implementations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition for resource-dependent performance comparisons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Elapsed times support a direct speed comparison only under sufficiently comparable execution environments and concurrency policies. Otherwise the comparison must declare an alternative accounting measure, such as evaluations or core-seconds, and report parallelism and included overhead. No single normalization is universally equivalent to elapsed time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heterogeneous execution requires a declared resource measure and disclosure of concurrency and overhead.
assumptions_latex: The estimand contains a resource-dependent performance measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{materially heterogeneous unnormalized times do not support an algorithm-only speed claim}.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Accounting Comparability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions for interpreting a contrast between solver pipelines.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two solver results are directly comparable for a declared estimand when they use equivalent mathematical instances, a common outcome definition, compatible feasibility and certificate semantics, and a resource-accounting rule appropriate to that estimand. Differences in information, preprocessing, hardware, concurrency, or overhead do not automatically invalidate a comparison, but they change or qualify the estimand and must be disclosed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-solver comparability is relative to a declared comparison target and requires common instance, outcome, certificate, and resource semantics.
assumptions_latex: The comparison states whether it concerns algorithms, configured solvers, or complete solver-information pipelines.
All reported outcomes are parsed under the same declared semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{common semantics plus disclosed pipeline differences}\Longrightarrow\text{interpretable estimand-relative contrast}.
knowledge_statements.title: Estimand-Relative Cross-Solver Comparability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretation boundary when tested solvers receive different information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If one solver receives derivatives, reformulations, starting points, reference values, or structural annotations unavailable to another, the experiment compares the resulting solver-information pipelines. It cannot support an algorithm-only attribution unless the information effect is controlled separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unequal supplied information changes the comparison target from algorithms alone to complete pipelines.
assumptions_latex: The asymmetric information can affect search, bounds, or termination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{undisclosed information asymmetry}\Longrightarrow\text{invalid algorithm-only attribution}.
knowledge_statements.title: Information-Asymmetry Boundary
Cross-Solver Comparability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which performance outcomes from different solvers are comparable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solvers \(a\) and \(b\) are directly comparable on instance set \(\mathcal I\) only when both receive mathematically equivalent instances, identical admissible information, equal resource limits under a common accounting rule, and the same feasibility, optimality-gap, termination, and failure definitions. For minimization, reported bounds must use the convention \(L_{s,i}\le f_i^\star\le U_{s,i}\). If preprocessing, parallelism, or external evaluations are permitted, their resource costs must be included identically. Comparisons violating any condition must be stratified or explicitly qualified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solver results are directly comparable only under equivalent instances, information, budgets, accounting, tolerances, bound conventions, and failure definitions.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal I\) is common to both solvers.
\(L_{s,i}\le f_i^\star\le U_{s,i}\) whenever solver \(s\) reports valid bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the stated conditions, differences in recorded outcomes are interpretable under one common evaluation protocol.

notation.meaning: global optimum value of instance i
valid lower bound reported by solver s
feasible upper bound reported by solver s

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: common instances, budgets, accounting, tolerances, and status definitions are necessary for fair solver comparison

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but a benchmarking source is required for the complete comparability criteria. The phrase “only when” presents every listed item as necessary, including identical admissible information, which may be too strong without a precisely defined comparison objective.

children.title: Certificate-Aware Reporting
children.top_down_role: Reporting conventions that distinguish solution quality from certification strength.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound reporting rule for certified minimization gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a report contains compatible verified bounds \(L\le f^\star\le U\), then it may report the absolute certified gap \(G=U-L\). A claim of absolute \(\varepsilon\)-global completion is justified when \(G\le\varepsilon\). A feasible point without a verified lower bound reports primal quality only; a lower bound without a verified feasible point reports bound progress only.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only compatible verified upper and lower bounds support a certified absolute gap and completion claim.
assumptions_latex: \(L\le f^\star\le U\) has been independently validated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U-L\le\varepsilon\Longrightarrow U-f^\star\le\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.title: Absolute-Gap Reporting Rule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for relative or mixed gap reporting near a zero scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A normalized gap depends on its declared scale. Division by \(|U|\), \(|L|\), or another scale may be undefined at zero or unstable near zero. A report using a relative or mixed gap must therefore state its formula and zero-scale rule; without them, only the finite absolute gap \(U-L\) has an invariant interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relative gaps require an explicit normalization and zero rule and are not interchangeable across conventions.
assumptions_latex: \(L\le f^\star\le U\) are finite verified bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{relative-gap claims are convention-dependent; }U-L\text{ is absolute}.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative-Gap Convention Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Report representation separating solver claims from verified evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each run, a certificate-aware report stores the candidate point and objective, feasibility status, reported lower bound, provenance or proof object, validation status of every claim, termination reason, and the protocol-declared gap fields. Missing, rejected, and unverified claims remain distinguishable. Only compatible verified bounds \(L\le f^\star\le U\) may be used to report a certified gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate-aware report records solution, bound, provenance, and validation fields without conflating solver claims with verified evidence.
assumptions_latex: The report identifies the mathematical instance and tolerance conventions.
Validation status is recorded separately from the solver's claimed status.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{certified gap field is populated only from verified }L\le f^\star\le U.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Aware Report Schema
Certificate-Aware Reporting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Report schema separating feasible values, valid bounds, and certified completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization run, a certificate-aware report records \((\hat x,U,L,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}},\sigma)\), where verified feasibility gives \(U=f(\hat x)\), a valid relaxation or proof object gives \(L\le f^\star\), and \(\sigma\) identifies which claims were independently checked. Certified \(\varepsilon\)-global completion may be reported only if \[U-L\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,|U|,|L|\}.\] A feasible point without a valid lower bound certifies only primal quality; a lower bound without a feasible point certifies only dual progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reports distinguish feasible solutions, valid lower bounds, and verified gap closure; only the last supports a certified global-completion claim.
assumptions_latex: \(L\le f^\star\le U\) whenever both reported bounds are certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed gap test certifies the declared absolute-relative global optimality tolerance.

source_refs.locator: 2.5 Local, Global, epsilon-Global Minima p. 57

review_flags: the exact mixed absolute-relative reporting convention requires dedicated support

source_witnesses.locator: 2.5 Local, Global, epsilon-Global Minima p. 57

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited section may support epsilon-global optimality generally, but it does not establish this exact mixed absolute-relative gap formula or verification-status schema. The record describes a reporting representation rather than a certificate itself, so the selected content kind also requires correction or explicit rationale.

children.title: Certificate-Aware Evaluation
children.top_down_role: Navigation container for separating feasible quality, bound quality, and proven completion.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluation that separates primal quality, bound quality, and proven completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization run, certificate-aware evaluation records separately: a verified feasible value \(U\), a verified global lower bound \(L\), and whether a protocol-declared completion test has been verified. An unavailable or rejected component remains missing rather than being imputed. When compatible certified bounds exist, \(L\le f^\star\le U\) and \(U-L\) bounds incumbent suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certificate-aware evaluation keeps feasible quality, lower-bound quality, and certified completion as distinct outcomes.
assumptions_latex: All combined quantities concern the same mathematical instance and tolerance conventions.
Any value called verified has passed the protocol's validation procedure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\le f^\star\le U\Longrightarrow 0\le U-f^\star\le U-L.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Aware Evaluation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary on interpreting uncertified solver outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An objective value from an unverified point is not a certified upper bound, and an estimate lacking a validity argument is not a certified global lower bound. Neither may enter a certified gap, and a termination label alone does not establish global completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unverified objectives, estimates, and labels cannot substitute for certified primal or lower-bound evidence.
assumptions_latex: The evaluation makes a global solution-quality claim for a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{certified gap use requires verified }L\le f^\star\le U.
knowledge_statements.title: Unverified-Outcome Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial order for comparing certificate-aware outcomes without collapsing missing components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For compatible minimization reports, an outcome \((U_1,L_1,c_1)\) weakly dominates \((U_2,L_2,c_2)\) when every compared component is available, \(U_1\le U_2\), \(L_1\ge L_2\), and \(c_1\ge c_2\) for the protocol's ordered completion statuses. Outcomes with opposing improvements or unavailable components are not totally ordered without an additional declared aggregation rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Better primal bounds, better lower bounds, and stronger completion evidence define only a partial order unless an aggregation rule is declared.
assumptions_latex: The reports use the same instance, validation rules, and completion-status order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: U_1\le U_2,\ L_1\ge L_2,\ c_1\ge c_2\Longrightarrow (U_1,L_1,c_1)\succeq(U_2,L_2,c_2).
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate-Evidence Dominance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Running-best representation of compatible verified primal and lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\bar U_k=\min_{j\le k}U_j\) over available verified feasible values and \(\bar L_k=\max_{j\le k}L_j\) over compatible verified global lower bounds. Then \(\bar U_k\) is nonincreasing, \(\bar L_k\) is nondecreasing, and \(\bar U_k-\bar L_k\) is nonincreasing whenever both are available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Running-best verified primal and lower bounds give a monotone certificate-progress trace.
assumptions_latex: Every combined bound is verified and refers to the same problem and tolerance conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bar U_{k+1}\le\bar U_k,\qquad \bar L_{k+1}\ge\bar L_k.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Verified Progress Trace

children.title: Global Optimization Failure-Boundary Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Boundaries where modeling, bounding, search, certification, or chapter ownership changes materially.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Global Optimization: Theory, Algorithms, and Applications
